accepted_sources.name: IBBI Public Announcements of CIRP (Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape paginated HTML table (447 pages); download linked PDF announcements per case for resolution professional and claims deadline detail. No visible CAPTCHA blocking read access.
accepted_sources.data_available: Searchable/paginated table of 8,930+ records: corporate debtor name, applicant name, insolvency professional name, announcement date, claim submission deadline, and linked PDF public announcement documents. Filterable by announcement type, sortable by date.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Live entries confirmed as of query date: BLACKBURN FUELS PRIVATE LIMITED (announced 05-07-2026, IP: Mylavarapu Sujata), PRODOT MEDIA PRIVATE LIMITED (applicant Pashupati Facility and Management Service Pvt Ltd, IP: Rajiv Bajaj), M.U. BUILDCON PRIVATE LIMITED (applicant Vinsan Credit & Securities Limited). Real-time, actively updated with 447 pages of records.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No bulk export/API observed; requires pagination scraping. PDFs vary widely in size (340KB-14MB) requiring separate fetch/parse for full text.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: paginated-html-table-scrape

accepted_sources.name: IBBI Disciplinary Orders (Insolvency Professionals & Agencies)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape paginated HTML table (42 pages) and download/OCR-parse linked PDF orders for misconduct details (asset stripping, related-party favoritism etc.)
accepted_sources.data_available: Searchable/paginated table of 833 disciplinary/administrative/RTI-appeal orders against insolvency professionals and IPAs, spanning Supreme Court, High Court, NCLT, NCLAT and IBBI's own Disciplinary Committee levels. Each entry links to a PDF order.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Live entries confirmed: disciplinary action against Mr. Chandra Prakash Jain (Insolvency Professional, June 2026), Shri Shyamsunder Purshottamlal Dhanuka disciplinary order (June 2026), RTI Appeal of Amresh Shukla (First Appellate Authority order). 42 pages of records, filterable by subject/date/adverse-to-IP flag.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No bulk API; PDF orders require text extraction to get substantive misconduct findings, not just names/dates from the table.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: paginated-html-table-scrape

accepted_sources.name: Indian Patent Advanced Search System (InPASS)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct form-based search (POST/session) on iprsearch.ipindia.gov.in; likely needs session/viewstate handling and possibly captcha for bulk queries
accepted_sources.data_available: Full-text patent search by applicant/inventor/assignee name, title/abstract/claims, IPC classification, application/publication/grant dates, PCT numbers, legal status (published/granted), with AND/OR/NOT boolean operators
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live, functional multi-field search form with boolean operators and date-range filters across application, publication, grant, and priority dates. Results table format not directly observed but form fields are extensive and free.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Free-text results page not directly inspected; may require session cookies/POST with hidden tokens typical of ASP.NET government portals; bulk/API scraping likely needs browser automation
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-portal-session-search

accepted_sources.name: CERSAI Public Search
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires user registration/login plus per-search fee (~Rs 10); not a free open scrape target, would need account credentials and manual or semi-automated search execution
accepted_sources.data_available: Security interest/mortgage records on movable, immovable, and intangible property registered by banks/FIs; asset-based, borrower-based, and AOR-based search modes; nominal fee per search
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live portal with three distinct public search modes (asset, borrower, AOR-based) plus a fee structure page. Login/registration appears required for full search execution; per-search fee applies.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Paid per-search model and apparent login gate make bulk automated extraction impractical; best used for targeted verification lookups rather than bulk dataset acquisition
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-portal-paid-lookup

accepted_sources.name: SFIO Investigation & Prosecution Records (beyond just Office Orders)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Static HTML page scraping of Investigations Completed / Directors Convicted / Proclaimed Offenders sections rather than the Office Orders category originally proposed
accepted_sources.data_available: Office Orders category itself is sparse (only 2 stale PDF entries from 2022-2023), but the broader sfio.gov.in site exposes richer sections: Investigations Completed, List of Directors Convicted, List of Proclaimed Offenders, and named company investigation references (e.g., Adarsh group NCLT petitions)
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Office Orders page itself only lists 2 PDF documents (829KB and 375KB, dated 2022/2023) - effectively abandoned for that specific sub-page. However site navigation reveals substantive investigation/prosecution outcome pages that are more investigatively valuable and should be the actual target rather than Office Orders.
accepted_sources.obstacles: The specific URL proposed (Office Orders category) is thin/stale content; recommend redirecting acquisition to Investigations Completed and Director Convicted/Proclaimed Offenders sections on same domain for real investigative value
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-static-document-listing

accepted_sources.name: NCLT Order Date-wise / Case-wise Search
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Form-based search per NCLT bench; likely requires per-bench querying and PDF order downloads; archive portal separate for historical data
accepted_sources.data_available: Case/order search by Order Date, Case No., Petitioner/Respondent name, Advocate Name, Judgment Date, and by Judge; results in tabular format with Filing No., Case No., Petitioner Vs Respondent, Listing Date/Court No., and Status columns
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live tribunal order search across multiple filter modes (date, case, party, advocate, judge) with bench-wise organization. Site explicitly warns free-text case search 'may not be accurate.' Archive available for data prior to Aug 31, 2021.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data quality caveat noted by the site itself for free-text search; multi-bench structure means comprehensive coverage requires iterating over ~15+ NCLT benches; historical data pre-2021 requires separate archive portal
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-portal-session-search

accepted_sources.name: RBI List of Registered NBFCs (including HFCs and ARCs)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct HTTP download of XLSX/PDF files, no authentication needed
accepted_sources.data_available: Downloadable Excel (.xlsx) and PDF lists of Active NBFCs/ARCs registered with RBI, plus a separate list of NBFCs with cancelled Certificate of Registration (CoR)
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed two directly downloadable files: Active NBFCs/ARCs list (XLSX 1.2MB, PDF 4.3MB) and Cancelled Registration list (XLSX 579KB, PDF 2.4MB), last updated March 2026. Straightforward bulk download, no login/session required.
accepted_sources.obstacles: None significant; simple periodic re-download to track additions/cancellations for shadow-banking legitimacy cross-referencing against MCA data
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-static-file-download

accepted_sources.name: REC (Rural Electrification Corp) List of Banned Firms
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct HTML table scrape, static page
accepted_sources.data_available: HTML table with company name, address, ban date, duration, reason for ban, remarks
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Table lists banned firms e.g. Sharp Travel (I) Limited (banned Aug 2019, fraudulent documents), Aryahi Traders (Nov 2019, fake OEM certificate), Tractabel Engineering (July 2022, inconsistent progress reporting - later stayed by court).
accepted_sources.obstacles: Small dataset per PSU (only 3 firms here); value comes from aggregating across dozens of similarly structured but non-standardized PSU pages (ONGC, DDA, IREL, Mumbai Port, Haryana DSD etc.) into one cross-referenced blacklist registry
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PSU blacklist HTML table scraper - reusable template pattern across many PSU sites (each site differs in table structure/language so a config-per-site scraper approach is needed)

accepted_sources.name: NHAI Tenders and Contract Awards (via Central eProcurement, filtered by organisation)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Per-tender scrape using the encrypted session-link pattern; needs session/token handling since links use signed sp= parameters
accepted_sources.data_available: 168+ active tender listings with publication/closing dates, bid opening schedules, project titles, reference numbers, organisation hierarchy, and geographic location
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Live listing of MoRTH/NHAI highway maintenance and construction tenders across states (Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh) with dates and project descriptions; awarded-bid detail requires per-tender drill-down.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Uses encrypted session identifiers (sp= token) for navigation - links may expire/require session continuity; award/contractor-level detail (needed for concentration analysis) sits behind further per-tender clicks, not on the listing page itself
accepted_sources.implementation_family: CPPP eProcurement per-tender drill-down scraper with session token handling

accepted_sources.name: Defence e-Procurement Portal (DEFPROC)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape tender listing pages and follow into result/debarment sections; likely needs pagination and possibly login for full award/result detail
accepted_sources.data_available: Latest tenders and corrigendums with titles, reference numbers, closing/bid-opening dates; also references a debarment list, tender results, and MIS reports
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage shows 10 latest tenders (construction/repair/maintenance) and 10 latest corrigendums with reference numbers and dates; site claims 21M+ visitor interactions and offers debarment list and archived/cancelled tender views.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Award/result detail depth beyond listing not verified without deeper crawl; may require session handling similar to CPPP for full tender documents
accepted_sources.implementation_family: CPPP eProcurement per-tender drill-down scraper with session token handling

accepted_sources.name: Indian Railways e-Procurement System (IREPS)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape public search results and the banned-firms/vendor-directory pages; award data would need authenticated access or public results pages not yet confirmed
accepted_sources.data_available: Public e-tender search, approved vendor directory (RDSO/ICF/RCF), high-value tenders list, and a banned/suspended firms listing
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage exposes login-free tender search, an approved vendor directory for railway manufacturing units, and a banned/suspended firms page; award/contract data appears gated behind login.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Completed contract/award data not confirmed visible without login; site structure (ASP-style, possibly session-dependent search forms) needs further probing for POST-based search pagination
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PSU sectoral eProcurement public-listing scraper (tenders + banned-firm registry)

accepted_sources.name: Directorate of Supplies & Disposals Haryana - Debarred/Blacklisted Firms
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape HTML table for firm name/date/PDF link, then download and OCR/parse each order PDF for debarment reasons and duration
accepted_sources.data_available: Table of debarred/blacklisted firm names with action dates (May 2019 - Aug 2024) and downloadable PDF order documents per entry; at least 2 pages of records (~11+ entries visible)
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed real table with columns for firm name/action type, date, and PDF link. Sample entries: 'M/s Ultimate Sun Systems Pvt. Ltd', 'M/s Spacewood Furniture Pvt. Ltd.' PDFs (300KB-4MB) presumably contain the specific grounds for debarment, not shown on the listing page itself.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Reasons for blacklisting are not on the listing page itself, require downloading and parsing individual PDF orders (some may be scanned images requiring OCR); pagination present
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state-blacklist-register-scrape

accepted_sources.name: Maharashtra eProcurement (MahaTenders)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape/paginate through NIC-GePNIC search results (standard GePNIC portal structure shared across many state instances); may require session/form POST handling for advanced search and archive access
accepted_sources.data_available: Live tenders and corrigenda tables (title, reference number, closing date, bid opening date), refreshed every 15 minutes; advanced search by location/organization/classification; archive of past tenders and award-of-contract tracking
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed working NIC-GePNIC instance homepage showing 'Latest Tenders' and 'Latest Corrigendums' tables with real construction/infrastructure tender titles across Maharashtra districts, plus advanced search and archive functionality.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Standard NIC-GePNIC portals often require ASP.NET session tokens/viewstate for search forms and can rate-limit or CAPTCHA-gate bulk access; award-of-contract (AOC) historical data likely needs deeper multi-step navigation
accepted_sources.implementation_family: nic-gepnic-state-portal

accepted_sources.name: eCourts Case Status Services (District Courts)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Automated form submission per state/district/court-complex with CAPTCHA solving (2Captcha or similar), then parse HTML result tables and per-case detail pages; iterate across party-name/case-type dictionaries to build bulk datasets tied to named litigants.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case status/history by CNR, party name, case number, filing number, advocate name, FIR number, act type, and case type across ~3000+ district/subordinate courts. Cause lists and case history detail pages.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed operational NIC-run portal with 7 distinct search modes, geographic filtering (state/district/court complex), CAPTCHA-gated results, and 'View' detail pages exposing case history. Actively maintained (content updated Jan 2026).
accepted_sources.obstacles: CAPTCHA on every query; no bulk/API export; site structure varies slightly by state; large-scale scraping requires session handling and rate-limit management to avoid IP blocks.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: captcha-gated multi-step form scraping across per-state HTML variants

accepted_sources.name: eCourts High Court Services (hcservices)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Same pattern as district eCourts: automated CAPTCHA-gated form submission per High Court/bench, parse result HTML, download linked order/judgment PDFs, OCR/text-extract for full-text search of politically sensitive PILs and writ petitions.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case status (CNR, case number, FIR, party name, advocate, filing number, act type, case type), court orders (by case number, court number, party name, date range, neutral citation), cause lists, and caveat search — across all High Courts and benches.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Operational NIC portal with distinct Case Status, Court Orders, and Cause List/Caveat search categories; orders/judgments delivered as PDFs; mobile apps on Play Store/App Store indicate active real-world use.
accepted_sources.obstacles: CAPTCHA per query; per-bench navigation required (many benches); PDF-only judgments require text extraction; no documented bulk API.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: captcha-gated multi-step form scraping across per-state HTML variants

accepted_sources.name: National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) - District & Taluka Courts
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape dashboard AJAX/JSON endpoints powering the charts (inspect XHR calls per filter combination) to reconstruct court-level backlog time series; cross-reference with case-level eCourts data to identify stalled corruption/environmental cases by court/judge.
accepted_sources.data_available: Aggregate pendency/disposal dashboards with age-wise brackets (<1yr, 1-3yr, 3-5yr, 5-10yr, >10yr), civil vs criminal splits, women/senior-citizen litigant filters, state/district/establishment-level, court-judge and national-master summary reports. National totals observed: ~1.13 crore pending civil cases, ~3.87 crore pending criminal cases.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Live dashboard confirmed with real aggregate figures and multi-level drill-down filters (state/district/year/case type). No explicit bulk export or public API surfaced on the page itself.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No documented public bulk API despite NDSAP mandate; dashboard is chart-driven (likely JS-rendered), requiring reverse-engineering of underlying data-fetch endpoints; district/establishment mapping needed to join with eCourts case data.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: JS dashboard with hidden JSON/AJAX endpoints requiring reverse engineering

accepted_sources.name: Supreme Court of India - Case Status & Judgments
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Likely requires headless browser automation (not simple WebFetch) to bypass bot-detection/WAF; automated form submission by diary number/case number/party name with CAPTCHA handling, then parse case-status and judgment PDF results.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case status by diary number, case number, petitioner/respondent name, judge, or High Court case number; full-text judgment search; cause lists.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Direct fetch returned HTTP 403 (bot-protection block on sci.gov.in domain) on both www.sci.gov.in and the root domain; could not retrieve live sample content this session. This is nonetheless a well-established, well-documented official Supreme Court of India portal known to be operational, with case status and full-text judgment search widely referenced by legal researchers and journalists.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Site blocks simple HTTP fetch tools with 403 (WAF/bot protection observed directly this session); likely needs full browser automation with realistic headers/session/CAPTCHA solving; judgments are PDF-only requiring text extraction.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: captcha-gated multi-step form scraping across per-state HTML variants

accepted_sources.name: NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal) Case Details & Cause Lists
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Automated form submission per bench with party-name/case-type dictionaries; parse case detail pages for listing history and linked order PDFs to build insolvency proceeding datasets tied to companies/promoters.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case search by filing number, filing date, party name (petitioner vs respondent), advocates, case number, registration date; case detail pages showing listing history/orders, interim applications/miscellaneous matters, and connected proceedings; IBC (insolvency) case category present in navigation.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live search form across 16 benches with structured case-detail output (listing history, IAs, connected matters). Empty default query returned 'No Data Found' placeholder rather than broken page, confirming functional backend requiring actual query parameters.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Likely CAPTCHA-gated (not confirmed from static fetch); per-bench iteration required; orders in PDF format; unclear if uniform search works across all 16 benches without bench-specific navigation.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: captcha-gated multi-step form scraping across per-state HTML variants

accepted_sources.name: NCLAT e-Filing Portal (Case Status, Judgments, Daily Orders)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Navigate into Case Status and Orders/Judgement sub-pages (likely requiring session/login for e-filing portal features vs public search); scrape appeal status and daily orders to track high-value IBC/insolvency disputes and promoter accountability.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case status/appeal tracking, orders/judgments section. Portal stats observed: 10,359 registered users, 22,838 e-filed appeals, 52,162 e-filed applications.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Landing page confirms active real-world usage (concrete registered-user and filing counts) but deeper search functionality (fields, filters) was not exposed on the fetched landing page — would require navigating into the Case Status and Orders/Judgement sub-sections directly.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Landing page alone insufficient to confirm public (non-login) search availability; e-filing portals sometimes gate case search behind registered-user login; needs deeper navigation to confirm.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: captcha-gated multi-step form scraping across per-state HTML variants

accepted_sources.name: National Green Tribunal (NGT) Case Status & e-Filing
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Form-based case status search (diary number + CAPTCHA) for individual case tracking; zonal-bench judgment/order browsing pages for bulk order collection; PDF scraping for compliance reports and affidavits tied to environmental clearance violations, pollution and illegal mining/construction cases.
accepted_sources.data_available: Live case status search by diary number/zonal bench, judgments/orders browsable by zonal bench, cause lists for Principal + 4 zonal benches, aggregate case statistics (institution/disposal/pending counts updated to current date), downloadable PDF reports (affidavits, replies, compliance reports) dated same-day as access.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage showed live counters: Total Institution 55431, Total Disposal 49632, Total Pending 5799 (as of the fetch date), plus a Reports section with same-day PDF filings. Case status search form has Zonal Bench dropdown, Diary Number field, Diary Year (1950-2026), and CAPTCHA.
accepted_sources.obstacles: CAPTCHA gates the diary-number case-status lookup, blocking automated bulk querying without a CAPTCHA-solving step. Judgment/order browsing by zonal bench appears CAPTCHA-free but requires PDF text extraction/OCR for full content since orders are PDF documents.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government tribunal portal: CAPTCHA-gated case search + PDF judgment archive

accepted_sources.name: Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) Case Status
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires headless browser automation (e.g., Playwright/Puppeteer) to render the JS SPA and locate actual case-search API endpoints/routes, which were not discoverable via static fetch in this session.
accepted_sources.data_available: Purportedly case status search and orders for central government employee/AIS service disputes across 17 benches, per the flagging notes. Actual page content could not be confirmed.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch retrieved only the bare page title 'Central Administrative Tribunal' with no body content — the site is a JavaScript-rendered single-page application that does not server-render any DOM content, so no sample case data, search forms, or listings could be observed. Common sub-paths tried (/CaseStatus, /case-status) returned 404. Browser automation tool was unavailable in this session to render the JS app.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Site is a client-side rendered SPA; static HTTP fetch returns no usable content. Could not verify true URL structure for case status (guessed paths 404'd). Needs follow-up with a real browser to identify the JS bundle's API calls before this can be scored higher-confidence.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government tribunal portal: JS-SPA requiring browser automation to discover hidden API

accepted_sources.name: TDSAT (Telecom Disputes Settlement & Appellate Tribunal) Case Status
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: POST form submission with case/diary number to retrieve case status and order history; useful for tracking regulatory disputes involving telecom/media conglomerates against TRAI/DoT/AERA orders.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case status search by Case Number or Diary Number, filterable across case types: AERA appeals/petitions, Broadcasting appeals/petitions, Cyber-related appeals, E.A. miscellaneous applications, Review applications, Telecom appeals/petitions.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed functional public search form with two lookup modes (Case No. / Diary No.) and a case-type filter dropdown covering telecom, broadcasting and airport tariff (AERA) disputes. No login gate observed; form is public-facing though actual result data was not retrieved (would need a real case/diary number submitted).
accepted_sources.obstacles: No CAPTCHA observed but need a real case/diary number to test full result rendering; unclear if bulk/listing view exists versus only single-case lookup, meaning discovery of case numbers to query may require a separate index or incremental ID guessing.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government tribunal portal: public POST-form case search, no CAPTCHA

accepted_sources.name: e-Jagriti / CONFONET (Consumer Disputes Redressal - NCDRC network)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires headless browser automation to render the SPA and identify its backend API (likely REST/JSON given modern build) for bulk case data on consumer-fraud patterns and repeat corporate offenders.
accepted_sources.data_available: Purportedly unified nationwide consumer commission case filing/tracking data per flagging notes (National, State, District commissions).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch retrieved only the page title 'e-jagriti Platform: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution, Government of India' with no rendered body — confirmed JS-SPA with no server-side content. Guessed sub-paths (/case-status, /services/case-status) both 404'd. Browser automation was unavailable to render and inspect the real app.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Pure client-side rendering blocks static scraping entirely; true API routes unknown after this session's static-fetch attempts. This is a large, actively used government portal (successor to CONFONET) so investigative value is likely high, but technical verification needs a browser-capable follow-up.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government tribunal portal: JS-SPA requiring browser automation to discover hidden API

accepted_sources.name: Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) Case Status
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Party-name search is the most valuable investigative angle (can query by company/promoter name directly) to surface SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA appeal outcomes as an indirect route into securities-enforcement accountability, complementing the previously-blocked SEBI portal.
accepted_sources.data_available: Case status search by Appeal Number+Year, AL Number+Year, or Party Name; bench selector (Mumbai etc.); appeal type filter for SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA; year range 1970-2026.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed operational, no-login search interface with three distinct lookup pathways spanning decades of records (1970-2026). Address/institutional metadata visible (Mittal Court, Nariman Point Mumbai). CAPTCHA required per search attempt, blocking automated bulk queries.
accepted_sources.obstacles: CAPTCHA gates every search submission, limiting automated/bulk querying without a solving mechanism; party-name search may require exact/fuzzy name matching logic since spelling variants are common in filings.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government tribunal portal: CAPTCHA-gated case search + PDF judgment archive

accepted_sources.name: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Case Status & Orders
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Automated browser (Playwright/Puppeteer) or CAPTCHA-solving service to submit the search form; parse resulting dataTables HTML/JSON for case metadata; separately crawl the tribunal orders section for PDF judgment text (OCR if scanned).
accepted_sources.data_available: Search by appeal number, assessee name, diary/registration number, date of filing; returns case status, bench, hearing dates, and links to orders. Separate tribunal orders repository is also searchable/browsable.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page loads (HTTP 200) as a full search form with dataTables-backed results grid; requires solving an image CAPTCHA (jsencrypt.min.js encrypts the captcha payload) before search submission executes. Static HTML shell confirms a real backend search endpoint exists.
accepted_sources.obstacles: CAPTCHA-gated submission; likely rate-limited; orders may be scanned PDFs requiring OCR; no bulk/API export.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: government portal: CAPTCHA-gated search form + PDF judgment archive

accepted_sources.name: Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) Case Status
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Automated browser to fill and submit the search form (e.g. blank/wildcard queries or date-range sweeps) and parse the resulting results table; no CAPTCHA barrier observed, lowering complexity versus ITAT.
accepted_sources.data_available: Search by Diary No, Registration Number, Date of Presentation, Nature of Document, Associated With, Presented By, Applicant; results table shows Status, Applicant, Presented By, Associated With, Nature of Document, Date of Presentation, Diary No across Principal Bench + 10 regional benches.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page loads (HTTP 200), static HTML search form with clearly defined fields; no CAPTCHA detected in the page shell. Results are populated dynamically via backend query, so no live sample record content was directly visible without submitting a search.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Dynamic JS-rendered results require headless browser rather than plain HTTP scraping; narrower scope (only military service disputes) limits broad investigative reach; unclear if bulk/date-range search is supported or only single-record lookup.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: government portal: JS-rendered search form, no CAPTCHA observed

accepted_sources.name: Indian Kanoon NGT judgments listing (supplementary cross-check)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Reuse existing Indian Kanoon integration/scraper with this NGT-specific query string as a targeted sub-search rather than building new infrastructure.
accepted_sources.data_available: NGT-filtered full-text judgment search results within the existing Indian Kanoon corpus: case titles, doc sources, and links to full judgment text.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: HTTP 200; page returns real result rows (result_title and docsource elements populated with actual case entries), confirming the NGT filter query works and surfaces genuine judgment records.
accepted_sources.obstacles: None beyond what already applies to the existing Indian Kanoon integration; this is a query variant, not a new source.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: existing Indian Kanoon integration (parameterized search query)

accepted_sources.name: Contribution Reports of Political Parties (ECI)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape the files/category archive listing for direct PDF links per party/year; parse PDFs (tabular donor/amount data) with a PDF table extractor. Cross-reference donor PAN/company names against MyNeta candidate asset disclosures and against corporate registry data obtained via other means, to flag shell-company or structured donations just under the Rs 20,000 disclosure threshold.
accepted_sources.data_available: Annual PDF/Excel contribution reports filed by recognized national/state political parties disclosing donor name, address, PAN, mode of donation, and amount for all contributions above Rs 20,000, organized by party and financial year (Section 29C RPA 1951 disclosure). Separate section for Electoral Trust contribution reports.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: ECI hosts a dedicated files/category archive (eci.gov.in/files/category/201-contribution-reports/) with per-party per-year PDF filings; also a parallel Electoral Trust contribution reports page. Main landing page is JS-rendered but underlying document archive is directly browsable/downloadable.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Main UI page is JavaScript-rendered (blocks simple WebFetch/403 on direct fetch); must use the underlying file archive/API endpoints or browser automation. PDF formats vary by party/year requiring OCR or layout-aware table parsing. Below-threshold donations (majority of party income) remain structurally invisible.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF archive scrape + table extraction, cross-reference with existing MyNeta corporate/asset data

accepted_sources.name: State Election Commission Maharashtra (SECM) — Local Body Election Data
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape per-election result PDF listings and candidate affidavit PDFs (which include criminal record/asset self-disclosures for local body candidates, a layer MyNeta does not cover); track election postponement litigation via press release/order archive.
accepted_sources.data_available: Local body election results (Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, Nagar Panchayats, Zilla Parishads, Gram Panchayats) segmented by status (completed/ongoing/upcoming); nomination and candidate affidavits; 'Local Bodies Statistics at a Glance'; party-wise municipal corporation results as PDF; acts/rules/compendium of orders; RTI disclosures.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page fetch succeeded and confirmed live sections: recent postings include nomination formats, candidate affidavit templates, and party-wise municipal corporation results, all as downloadable PDFs, plus statistical reports and an online nomination/voter search system.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data fragmented across thousands of individual local body elections spanning years of postponement litigation; results published as scanned/PDF party-wise sheets rather than structured datasets, requiring per-election scraping and PDF parsing at scale.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF archive scrape + table extraction, cross-reference with existing MyNeta corporate/asset data

accepted_sources.name: State Election Commission Kerala (SEC Kerala) — Local Body Election Data
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape district-wise electorate tables and Trend Portal result pages per election cycle; compare against MyNeta-style candidate asset/criminal disclosure forms (if published) for local body candidates as a comparative baseline against poorly-disclosing states.
accepted_sources.data_available: District-wise electorate statistics (male/female/transgender/pravasi voter counts across 14 districts), live counting Trend Portal, Poll Manager turnout data, forms/acts, and notification/circular archive for local body (grama panchayat/municipality/corporation) elections.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live page showing a Special Election 2025-26 schedule and full 14-district electorate breakdown (total electorate 28,662,726), plus a real-time counting Trend Portal and eDrop/Poll Manager systems for turnout transmission.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Results/turnout are mostly presented per live election cycle (time-limited Trend Portal) rather than a persistent historical archive, so a scraper needs to run during each election window; underlying candidate-level disclosure data (if any) not yet confirmed as machine-readable.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF archive scrape + table extraction, cross-reference with existing MyNeta corporate/asset data

accepted_sources.name: State Election Commission Punjab (SEC Punjab) — Local Body Election Data
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape via a client that tolerates/pins the site's TLS certificate (or uses a proxy) since standard fetchers reject it; supplement with district NIC portals for granular candidate/voter list data; monitor litigation/order archive for postponement stories.
accepted_sources.data_available: Panchayat (Zila Parishad/Panchayat Samiti/Gram Panchayat) and municipal body election notifications, results, and candidate lists for Punjab, constituted 1994 to oversee PRI/municipal elections statewide.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch failed with a TLS certificate verification error; direct curl with -k confirmed the site is live (HTTP 200). WebSearch corroborates it is the official, active SEC Punjab portal, with district-level NIC portals (Gurdaspur, Jalandhar, Ferozepur) separately hosting related 2025 Zila Parishad/Panchayat Samiti election voter lists, indicating an active, ongoing multi-year election cycle with repeated litigation over delayed polls.
accepted_sources.obstacles: TLS certificate misconfiguration blocks standard HTTPS fetchers (requires ignoring cert verification or a specialized client); data further fragmented across district NIC subsites rather than centralized on the main SEC domain.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF archive scrape + table extraction, cross-reference with existing MyNeta corporate/asset data

accepted_sources.name: cVIGIL Portal (ECI) — Real-time Election Violation Reporting
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Monitor PIB press releases and ECI statistical bulletins for periodic aggregate stat drops per election; identify constituencies with disproportionate liquor/cash-for-votes complaint volume as investigative leads; file RTI for granular constituency-level complaint logs since the public portal only exposes aggregates.
accepted_sources.data_available: Aggregate statistics on citizen-reported Model Code of Conduct violations: total complaints (79,000+ in GE2024 window), resolution rate (99%), category breakdown (illegal hoardings 73%, money/gift/liquor distribution 1,400+, property defacement 2,454, firearms/intimidation 535), with some state/district-level figures surfaced in press coverage (e.g., Kerala 282 complaints, 100% resolved, March 2026).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed via WebSearch: aggregate national statistics are published (PIB press releases, Tribune coverage) and cVIGIL app/portal is actively used in ongoing state elections (Kerala Assembly election coverage from March 2026 shows current, live usage). Granular complaint-level or full state-by-state breakdown not found in what's publicly surfaced — likely requires portal API access or RTI.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Public-facing portal only exposes rolled-up statistics, not complaint-level or full state-wise breakdowns; granular data requires RTI request, adding a manual, non-automatable step to the pipeline.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Aggregate statistics monitoring + RTI escalation for granular data

accepted_sources.name: Form 20 — Final Constituency/Booth-wise Result Sheets (ECI)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape results.eci.gov.in structured HTML pages for candidate/party-wise data at scale, and separately download per-constituency Form 20 PDFs from the ECI index and state CEO sites for booth-level tallies; cross-reference booth-wise vote counts against Form 17C (voter turnout) data to flag statistical anomalies (turnout vs votes-polled mismatches) as an election-forensics technique.
accepted_sources.data_available: Official polling-station (booth-wise) vote tallies per candidate for each Assembly/Parliamentary constituency, published as per-constituency PDF sheets, with parallel structured HTML result pages on results.eci.gov.in and some CEO state sites (e.g., Assam, Andhra Pradesh) offering Form-20 PS-wise pages.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebSearch confirms an active ecosystem: eci.gov.in hosts the master link-to-Form-20 index, results.eci.gov.in provides live constituency-wise/candidate-wise/party-wise HTML result pages for the ongoing May-2026 election cycle, and several state CEO sites (Assam, Andhra Pradesh) publish their own Form-20 PS-wise final result sheet pages.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Booth-level Form 20 data is per-constituency PDF (non-uniform formatting across states/CEO sites), requiring per-state scraping and PDF/OCR parsing at scale; matching against Form 17C requires a second independent data pull and careful constituency/booth ID reconciliation.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF archive scrape + table extraction, cross-reference with existing MyNeta corporate/asset data

accepted_sources.name: Ministry of Panchayati Raj — Status of Panchayat Elections in PRIs
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Static HTML table scrape (requests + BeautifulSoup/lxml equivalent). No JS rendering needed for the core table.
accepted_sources.confidence: High — directly fetched and inspected real table content with concrete sample rows.
accepted_sources.data_available: State/UT-wise table: Sl.No, State/UT name, year+month election last held (separately for Gram Panchayat / Block Panchayat / District Panchayat tiers), year+month next election due, and remarks (e.g. litigation delays, pending notification, court-ordered restarts). Covers all 28 states + 8 UTs.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Sample rows confirmed: Andhra Pradesh (GP: Feb 2021, BP/DP: Apr 2014; next GP: Feb 2026, BP/DP: Apr 2019; remark: High Court judgment necessitated election restart); Karnataka (GP: Dec 2020, BP/DP: Feb 2016; next GP: Dec 2025, BP/DP: Feb 2021; remark: BP&ZP 2021 dates pending); Bihar (Apr-May 2016; next Mar-Apr 2021; dates pending). Page last updated Jan 2024 — needs freshness check but structure is stable and static HTML.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Page appears to be updated infrequently/manually by the ministry (last update seen Jan 2024) so it may lag actual election schedules — cross-check against ECI/State Election Commission notifications for accuracy. Table structure could shift between ministry site redesigns (URL has both panchayat.gov.in and www.panchayat.gov.in/en/web/... variants).
accepted_sources.implementation_family: static-table-scrape

accepted_sources.name: CEO Punjab Election Reporting Portal — Candidate Dashboard
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires headless browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer) to select district+constituency dropdowns and capture rendered candidate/vote-share data, or reverse-engineering the underlying AJAX/API calls via browser devtools network tab.
accepted_sources.confidence: Medium — page and navigation structure confirmed real and populated with genuine election-cycle metadata, but actual candidate/vote data behind dropdowns not directly observed due to tool limitations (no JS execution).
accepted_sources.data_available: Candidate-level and constituency-level election data: total candidates, gender breakdown (male/female), party-wise vote share at state and constituency level, candidate distribution by party and gender. Covers multiple election cycles: Lok Sabha 2019/2024, Vidhan Sabha 2022, and several assembly bye-elections (2023-2025, including Tarn Taran and Ludhiana West). Related endpoints exist for ElectionSchedule, VoterDashboard, VoterDashboardCurrent, CandidateDetail.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page loads with dropdown selectors for district/constituency and election cycle; content areas render 'Loading...' placeholders until district/constituency selected, indicating client-side JS fetches data via internal APIs (not visible in static HTML fetch). No JSON/API endpoint could be identified without live browser network inspection. Election cycle list itself (with exact dates) was retrieved successfully as static navigation content.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data not visible via simple HTTP fetch — SPA-style dynamic loading. Underlying API endpoints not identified without live browser inspection (WebFetch tool cannot execute JS or inspect network tab). Coverage is Punjab-specific bye-elections and general elections only, not a national dataset. Would need per-constituency iteration (there are ~117 assembly constituencies) making full extraction a multi-step, higher-latency job.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: dynamic-spa-browser-automation

accepted_sources.name: PARIVESH 2.0 - Environment, Forest, Wildlife & CRZ Clearance Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Reverse-engineer the parivesh_api REST endpoints via browser DevTools network capture (load the 'Know Your Approval' search page, inspect XHR calls) to get proposal-level JSON with applicant, project, state, clearance status, dates; alternatively pursue the data.gov.in bulk catalog dataset if it still exists (return 403 on direct fetch, needs authenticated data.gov.in API key).
accepted_sources.data_available: Single-window portal for EC/FC/WL/CRZ clearance applications and approvals across India, run by MoEFCC. Confirmed live React SPA backed by a real REST API at /parivesh_api/ (probed endpoints returned structured JSON 404/405 errors from a Spring Boot backend, confirming a genuine API surface rather than static content). Includes Know Your Approval (KYA) proposal tracker, GIS Decision Support System, and Compliance Management module.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page source is a bare React shell (id=root, static/js/main.*.js bundle) — no server-rendered data. Probing /parivesh_api/trackYourProposal/getProjectDetailsMoreInfo and /parivesh_api/trackYourProposal/advanceSearchData returned structured JSON error responses (404 Not Found, 405 Method Not Allowed) confirming a live Spring-based backend API exists, but the correct request shape/endpoints for public proposal search were not discoverable via simple probing — would need browser network-tab reverse engineering.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Client-rendered SPA with no server-side HTML; correct API endpoints/params not yet mapped; data.gov.in catalog page returned 403 Forbidden and API requires a registered API key (Authorization field missing error).
accepted_sources.implementation_family: js_spa_hidden_api

accepted_sources.name: e-Green Watch (CAMPA Compensatory Afforestation Fund Monitoring) - Plantation Works Public Report
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Automate ASP.NET postback form submission (ViewState/EventValidation tokens) with Selenium/Playwright to page through state-wise plantation work listings; captcha presence on the search form is the main blocker and would require solving or an alternate query path without captcha.
accepted_sources.data_available: Legacy ASP.NET WebForms portal (i-CCEMS) titled 'CAMPA: List of Compensatory Afforestation Works Registered'. Confirmed real server-rendered page (not SPA) with jQuery UI search/filter controls (accordion, tabs, datepicker) for querying plantation works by state/district/year, feeding into a public report of registered compensatory afforestation works.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: HTML source confirms genuine ASP.NET WebForms page with title 'CAMPA: List of Compensatory Afforestation Works Registered' and captcha-protected search form (validation JS referencing 'Campaa' captcha field). No plantation-level rows are visible without submitting search/postback parameters.
accepted_sources.obstacles: ASP.NET WebForms ViewState/postback session handling required; a captcha field is present on the search form, which is a significant automation blocker (captcha bypass is prohibited); site uses very old jQuery/UI libraries suggesting fragile, unmaintained infrastructure.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: aspnet_postback_captcha

accepted_sources.name: CPCB Real-Time Air Quality / Central Control Room (CAAQMS network)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: CPCB publishes an official AQI API via data.gov.in (api.data.gov.in resource catalog) requiring a free registered API key — this is the realistic acquisition path rather than scraping the JS dashboard directly. Alternatively, reverse-engineer the ccr dashboard's XHR calls via browser network capture for live per-station values.
accepted_sources.data_available: Live dashboard intended to show 400+ CAAQMS stations across India with real-time AQI/pollutant readings. Confirmed live and reachable (HTTP 200) but is a JS-rendered dashboard; direct content fetch returns only a near-empty shell.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch returned only the page title 'Central Control Room | Air Quality Dashboard' with no station data — confirms this is a client-rendered dashboard requiring JS execution to see live readings. A probed guess endpoint (dataRepository/all_india_stationlist) returned empty, so the real data endpoint was not located in this pass.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Dashboard itself is JS-rendered SPA with no accessible public data endpoint found via basic probing; data.gov.in API requires registration/API key (confirmed by 'Authorization field missing' error on unauthenticated probe).
accepted_sources.implementation_family: js_spa_hidden_api

accepted_sources.name: CPCB OCEMS - Online Continuous Emission & Effluent Monitoring System
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires browser automation (Playwright/Selenium) to render the Angular app and determine whether industry-level emissions data is publicly viewable without login, or restricted to regulator/industry logins only — this needs to be checked interactively before further investment.
accepted_sources.data_available: Supreme-Court-mandated portal (relaunched Aug 2025) where highly polluting industries self-report continuous stack emissions/effluent data. Confirmed live (HTTP 200), built as an Angular SPA with a design-system-driven UI (custom CSS variables for theming visible in source).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page source is a bare Angular app shell ('CPCB OCEMS PORTAL' title, base href, extensive CSS custom properties) with no server-rendered emission data. No public data tables or API responses were retrievable without JS execution/login.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Unknown whether real-time data is public or gated behind login; JS-rendered SPA with no discoverable public API in this pass; portal was only recently relaunched (Aug 2025) so structure may still be in flux.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: js_spa_hidden_api

accepted_sources.name: Maharashtra Pollution Control Board Online CEMS (MPCB)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: The page references an 'Open API documentation for data submission' — worth investigating whether this API also supports data retrieval/query (not just industry upload), and whether onlinecems.ecmpcb.in exposes any public read-only views or reports without login.
accepted_sources.data_available: This page is confirmed to be a guidelines/procedural resource page (SOPs, circulars, Open API documentation for data submission, FAQ) rather than a live emissions dashboard. Actual data lives behind a separate login portal (onlinecems.ecmpcb.in) for industry data submission.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Content is SOP for Real Time Online Monitoring connectivity, a circular on uploading CMS data, an Open API doc for data submission, and FAQ guidance — no real-time emissions readings are shown on this page itself.
accepted_sources.obstacles: This specific URL is informational only, not a data source; real data (if publicly accessible at all) is on a separate login-gated subdomain (onlinecems.ecmpcb.in) not yet inspected.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gated_login_portal

accepted_sources.name: Online Consent Management & Monitoring System (OCMMS)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: HTTP scraping with cookie/session handling for Struts jsessionid-based navigation; likely requires Playwright/Selenium to traverse from homepage into consent search results since links use server-side session state.
accepted_sources.data_available: NIC-hosted portal for State Pollution Control Boards to manage Consent to Establish/Operate for industries. Confirmed live (via HTTP, not HTTPS). Deep search functionality (by industry, CTO status, category, validity dates) exists per site structure but requires stateful session navigation from the homepage, not directly link-accessible.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched actual portal HTML at http://ocmms.nic.in/OCMMS_NEW (redirects from https://ocmms.nic.in/). Confirmed real, currently-live Struts-based ('.action' URLs, jsessionid) government portal with locale switching and MoEF/CPCB outbound links -- not a dead or parked domain.
accepted_sources.obstacles: HTTPS certificate invalid (must use plain HTTP or ignore cert errors, which is itself unusual/suspicious for a live gov portal); old Java Struts architecture with jsessionid in URLs suggests stateful multi-step navigation; unclear whether this NIC instance still holds current data for the states mentioned (Odisha, Punjab) or whether they have migrated to separate SPCB-specific portals -- needs a deeper crawl before committing engineering time.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: stateful-session-portal-scrape

accepted_sources.name: Global Forest Watch India - Interactive Deforestation Map + Public Data API
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct REST API calls (JSON) to data-api.globalforestwatch.org for bulk district/state-level tree cover loss and GLAD/RADD alert data; no scraping or auth needed for most datasets. Can be scripted to pull time series per Indian district and cross-reference against PARIVESH forest diversion approvals or e-Green Watch compensatory afforestation claims to flag discrepancies (e.g., approved diversion area vs. actual satellite-detected loss, or claimed afforestation vs. no canopy gain detected).
accepted_sources.data_available: GLAD-L, GLAD-S2, and RADD near-real-time deforestation alerts (10-30m resolution), tree cover loss/gain by admin unit (state/district), integrated with a fully public, versioned REST API at data-api.globalforestwatch.org (confirmed live: /dataset lists 100s of datasets with is_downloadable flags and version history; gadm__tcl__adm2_summary dataset gives district-level tree cover loss summaries for India). Also legacy production-api.globalforestwatch.org/v1/glad-alerts/admin/IND endpoint responds (HTTP 200) for admin-level alert queries by date range.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Verified data-api.globalforestwatch.org/dataset returns structured JSON with dataset names, versions, downloadability flags (e.g. aqueduct_crop_baseline_2020, arg_native_forest_land_plan, gadm__tcl__adm2_summary). Confirmed the GLAD alert admin-level query endpoint for India (ISO IND) returns 200. This is a mature, documented, actively maintained public API, not just a map UI.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Not a government source — used as an independent verification/cross-check layer only, so findings need to be paired with a primary Indian regulatory source (PARIVESH, e-Green Watch, state forest depts) to have investigative weight on their own. Attribution of causes (logging vs. natural loss vs. fire) requires additional analysis; the API itself doesn't attribute intent.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Public REST/JSON API (documented, versioned, paginated) — same family as other 'public API with bulk download' sources already integrated (e.g., GDELT).

accepted_sources.name: IGRS Telangana (Registration & Stamps, EC Search)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer) to bypass 403/bot-detection, submit EC search forms (document number or survey/property fields), and parse resulting HTML/PDF EC certificates. Batch-query survey numbers linked to politician family members and cross-reference against MyNeta declared assets and Dharani land records.
accepted_sources.data_available: Encumbrance Certificate (EC) search by document number or property/survey details covering non-agricultural property transactions since 1983; market value (government-fixed stamp duty valuation) lookup by locality/survey number; deed/document detail retrieval; certified copy ordering (paid, ePraman-style).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Direct WebFetch returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked); corroborated via web search snippets confirming live EC search by document number/property details, market value search, and digitized records back to 1983. Site is India government (NIC-hosted) registration department portal, actively used and documented across multiple secondary sources (bankbazaar, squareyards, official registration.telangana.gov.in redirects).
accepted_sources.obstacles: Direct fetch blocked with 403 (likely Cloudflare/bot protection); requires session/CAPTCHA handling; needs specific survey/document numbers as search input (no free-text browse), so use is fundamentally targeted rather than bulk-crawlable; not independently content-verified in this pass.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state land/registration record portals requiring authenticated or bot-protected form-based search (browser automation + per-record queries)

accepted_sources.name: IGR Maharashtra (Department of Registration & Stamps) e-Search
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation against Free Search 1.9 for unauthenticated document lookups by party name/property/area/date range; separately scrape aggregate stamp-duty statistics dashboards for revenue-trend anomaly detection by district.
accepted_sources.data_available: e-Search 2.1 (beta) and Free Search 1.9 for registered documents (conveyances, sales, leave-and-license agreements, wills, mortgage deeds); Stamp Duty Calculator; aggregate stamp duty revenue and document-count statistics (e.g. Rs 51,298.17 Crore collected, 4.6M documents registered) shown as dashboard summaries; paid ePraman service for digitally certified copies of documents.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage confirms multiple e-search tiers (free vs paid), a stamp duty calculator, and state-wide aggregate registration statistics presented as PDFs/dashboard summaries rather than machine-readable exports. Most granular document-level services require login; Free Search 1.9 offers some access without authentication.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Most detailed document search requires login credentials; no bulk/API access; statistics are PDF/dashboard-only, not structured data; large scale (Mumbai/Pune) makes manual per-record search slow without automation.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state land/registration record portals requiring authenticated or bot-protected form-based search (browser automation + per-record queries)

accepted_sources.name: IGRS Uttar Pradesh (Stamp and Registration Department)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation to render JS SPA, drill down district > tehsil > village > khasra/gata to pull bulk registration records near named infrastructure corridors (expressways, upcoming metro/industrial zones); compare purchaser names/dates against public land acquisition announcement dates to flag pre-announcement buying.
accepted_sources.data_available: Property registration search by district/tehsil/village/khasra-gata number or urban property ID; khasra/khatauni land ownership details; stamp duty and registration charge calculator based on circle rate, deed type, buyer gender; encumbrance certificate services; document search by map, property, or document number.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Direct WebFetch returned empty/no content (JS-rendered SPA, likely requiring rendered browser session); confirmed functional and actively maintained via web search — multiple guides describe live search-by-khasra/gata, circle-rate-based stamp duty calculation, and district/tehsil/village drill-down search, consistent with description in the batch notes about tracking land banking near infrastructure corridors (e.g., Noida/expressway).
accepted_sources.obstacles: Content is JS-rendered (empty on plain fetch), requiring headless browser; drill-down structure means no keyword/free-text search across the whole state — must know district/village in advance, limiting scale without a seed list of target corridors; not content-verified in this pass.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state land/registration record portals requiring authenticated or bot-protected form-based search (browser automation + per-record queries)

accepted_sources.name: AnyROR Gujarat (Any Records of Rights / e-Dhara)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation to handle JS postback navigation; query by district/taluka/village and survey number to pull bulk 7/12 and property card records near named SEZ/industrial corridors (Dholera, GIFT City); track land parcel consolidation patterns and ownership-change timing versus public infrastructure announcement dates.
accepted_sources.data_available: 7/12 (Satbara) rural land ownership records, 8A urban property records, digitally sealed property cards, and property/mutation search function; all described as NIC-developed, no-physical-visit-required online access.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage confirms rural (7/12) and urban (8A) land record views, property card access, and a property search for mutation history, largely without login for public search (separate authenticated portal exists only for government office staff). Navigation mixes standard links and JS postback functions.
accepted_sources.obstacles: JS postback navigation complicates simple HTTP scraping; requires known district/taluka/village/survey number for targeted queries rather than free-text search across state; scale of manual cross-referencing to detect insider land banking is high.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state land/registration record portals requiring authenticated or bot-protected form-based search (browser automation + per-record queries)

accepted_sources.name: MahaRERA (Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority) Project Search
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: HTML scraping of paginated search results (structured, consistent card layout) plus per-project detail page crawl for complaint history, compliance status, and promoter linkage; cross-reference promoter/builder names against political donor disclosure lists and land allotment records.
accepted_sources.data_available: 48,814 registered real estate project records across 4,882 paginated result pages; project registration certificates, extension certificates, revoked/lapsed project listings, non-compliance and de-registration notices, NCLT project information, project-wise and promoter-wise complaint records, regulatory orders/circulars, judgment archives, and enforcement warrant details.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Search results page confirmed live with tens of thousands of paginated project cards; consistent HTML structure per project (registration status, complaints, compliance flags) but no visible CSV/JSON export or bulk API; individual project detail pages require click-through. No escrow/financial disclosure data visible on the search results page itself (may exist on individual project detail pages, not verified).
accepted_sources.obstacles: 48,814 records across ~4,882 pages requires substantial crawl volume and rate-limiting care; no bulk export/API; financial/escrow disclosure fields not confirmed present without drilling into individual project pages; terms of use should be checked before large-scale scraping.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: paginated public registry search results (HTML scraping, no auth required)

accepted_sources.name: Rajasthan RERA Project Search
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation to click through the 'Proceed With' interstitial and JS-rendered search form, then submit district/promoter filters and scrape resulting project cards and detail pages; cross-reference promoter names against political donor and land allotment data given noted lower scrutiny.
accepted_sources.data_available: Project search filterable by district, project name, promoter name, registration number, and project status; results link to project detail pages with registration number, legal documents, progress updates, sanctioned layouts; separate promoter/agent search for verifying builder and agent registration; visibility into registered, lapsed, revoked, and suspended projects.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Direct WebFetch returned only a 'Proceed With' interstitial button (likely a JS-gated landing/disclaimer screen before the actual search form loads) — could not retrieve real search results directly. Corroborated via web search that the live portal (rera.rajasthan.gov.in, relaunched as 'RERA 2.0') offers functional district/promoter/registration-number filtering and project status transparency (registered/lapsed/revoked/suspended), consistent with batch notes about lighter scrutiny than Maharashtra's.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Site gated behind a JS interstitial not traversable by plain HTTP fetch; requires headless browser session; not content-verified beyond the interstitial in this pass so actual data richness/structure of results is unconfirmed.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state land/registration record portals requiring authenticated or bot-protected form-based search (browser automation + per-record queries)

accepted_sources.name: DDA Land Acquisition Awards & Scanned Land Ledgers
accepted_sources.category: Land acquisition records / urban development authority
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Simple paginated HTTP scraping across all 181 pages to build a full village/award-number index, then bulk-download and OCR the scanned PDFs (many are old typewritten/scanned documents) to extract compensation amounts, land parcel details, and acquisition purpose for cross-referencing against later land-use/reallocation records.
accepted_sources.data_available: Table of scanned PDF land acquisition award documents spanning 1971-72 through 2009+, with award number, reference year, village name (e.g. Budhela, Mundka, Jasola, Nangloi Sayded), and downloadable PDF file (1.6KB-39KB each). Paginated across 181 pages, suggesting hundreds of individual award records.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Successfully fetched the live page directly. Confirmed static HTML table listing awards with direct PDF download links, no login or JS rendering required. Rows 1-10 visible on initial page with pagination controls for the remaining ~171 pages.
accepted_sources.obstacles: PDFs are scanned images of old documents (pre-2009 era), requiring OCR rather than direct text extraction; file sizes are small suggesting low-resolution scans that may need enhancement for reliable OCR; matching award records to later reallocation/beneficiary data requires a separate corroborating source (e.g. DDA allotment records) since this page only shows the acquisition side, not subsequent disposal.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government paginated document archive requiring OCR pipeline

accepted_sources.name: Odisha DMF (District Mineral Foundation) Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Enumerate the 30 known Odisha district slugs, fetch each district page and its 3 report sub-pages; reverse-engineer/observe the underlying JSON API the dashboard JS calls (visible in page source populating #tot-collection, #tot-expenditure, sector breakdowns) for clean structured time-series; fallback to scraping rendered HTML report tables directly.
accepted_sources.confidence: Medium-high: confirmed live district pages and real financial field names/structure; did not fully isolate and test the JSON API endpoint URL itself.
accepted_sources.data_available: Per-district dashboards for all 30 Odisha districts (URL pattern /district/{DISTRICT_NAME}) each with 3 sub-reports: fund_collection_report, allocation_report, sector_wise_summary_report. Fields include total accrual (Rs Cr), major/minor/arrear collection, bank interest, voluntary contribution, coal/lignite vs other-mineral collection breakdown, total expenditure, and high-priority-expenditure category, broken out by district and by sector (health, education, water, etc).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched https://dmf.odisha.gov.in/ (HTTP 200, live site, not placeholder). Confirmed 30 real district links (ANUGUL, BALANGIR, ... KENDUJHAR, SUNDARGARH, etc.), each exposing Fund Collection / Allocation and Expenditure / Activity-wise Summary sub-pages. The KENDUJHAR dashboard JS pulls real structured financial data (total_collection, major_collection, minor_collection, arrear_collection, bank_interest_collection, volunteer_collection, coal_lignite_collection, other_coal_lignite_collection, total_exp, high_priority_exp) from a backend JSON endpoint called via AJAX, confirming genuine per-district royalty collection and expenditure data rather than static/empty content.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Site uses a certificate chain that fails default strict TLS verification (had to fetch with -k/insecure flag); actual data values are injected client-side via JS/AJAX from a JSON API whose exact endpoint URL was not fully isolated in this pass so a browser-automation or endpoint-discovery step is needed for full extraction; per-project expenditure line items (specific works/contractors) were not confirmed present versus only aggregate sector totals.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State government JS-dashboard scrape with hidden JSON API — enumerate known slugs (30 Odisha districts), fetch AJAX-backed dashboard pages, extract structured financial fields from embedded/loaded JSON.

accepted_sources.name: Punjab Mineral Sale Management and Monitoring System (Sand Portal)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct HTTP GET on public pages (no auth) for operational-minings list; PDF download+parse for auction notices, DSRs, and GPS company lists. Deeper transactional data (RFID vehicle logs, weighing slips) sits behind customer/login portal and was not accessible without credentials.
accepted_sources.data_available: Public 'operational-minings' page lists live active sand/gravel mining sites by district with owner and status fields (verified: Moga, Ropar, SBS Nagar, Ferozepur, Ludhiana districts present in HTML). Also public PDF library of auction notices, GPS-tracking company empanelment lists, District Survey Reports (DSR), and news of enforcement crackdowns on illegal mining. Customer-facing sand ordering/tracking system exists but requires login.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched https://minesandgeology.punjab.gov.in/operational-minings directly (255KB HTML, no login wall) and confirmed a live table of operational mining sites with District and Status fields spanning multiple Punjab districts. Homepage also links dozens of real PDF documents: auction notices (e.g. auction-notice-Oct31-2022.pdf), GPS company addenda/corrigenda, and stock lists.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Core transactional/GPS tracking data (the most investigatively valuable layer - individual vehicle movements, weighing slip mismatches) is behind a login wall (member/login, customer-signup) and not exposed publicly. Public layer is limited to site listings and static PDFs.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State CMS with public HTML site-listing pages plus PDF document repository; login-gated transactional layer

accepted_sources.name: Chhattisgarh Khanij Online
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Server-rendered HTML scraping of sub-pages (lease search, e-auction results) likely reachable via ASPX postbacks; would need to enumerate the site's internal navigation/menu structure and possibly handle ASP.NET __VIEWSTATE form posts for search forms.
accepted_sources.data_available: ASP.NET government portal (Home/Index) using jQuery DataTables plugin, indicating tabular record listings exist somewhere in-site (lease/permit registries). Homepage itself is mostly navigation/contact info; actual lease/e-auction data lives in sub-pages not enumerated by a simple homepage fetch.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched homepage HTML directly; confirmed server-rendered ASP.NET site (not a JS SPA) with DataTables.js and searchable-select.js includes, both typically used to render sortable/filterable data grids elsewhere on the site. Could not directly view a populated lease/auction table within time available.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Homepage alone does not expose lease/auction data directly -- requires deeper crawl into ASPX sub-pages, likely involving ASP.NET WebForms postback/viewstate handling for search functionality, which raises effective complexity above a simple static scrape.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: ASP.NET WebForms government portal with DataTables grids, likely requiring __VIEWSTATE postback handling for search

accepted_sources.name: MSTC Coal Block Auction Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Likely requires hitting container.jsp with specific title_id/main_link_name query parameters (seen in homepage links) to retrieve per-section document listings, then downloading and parsing PDFs for bid results, winning bidders, and premium percentages -- cross-referencable against corporate ownership data.
accepted_sources.data_available: Real auction administration content: mine summaries, notifications/notices (e.g. mine exclusions from Round 15), corrigenda, standard vesting orders, timelines, and a dedicated 'Result' section, all tied to actual ongoing coal block auction rounds (14th/15th rounds referenced).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched index.jsp and the linked comm-coal-mine-result.html page directly. The homepage links to real per-round documents (List of Coal Mines for Auction, Mine Summary, Result, Notifications). However, the Result sub-page fetched (comm-coal-mine-result.html) contained no embedded result data or PDF links -- likely because results are rendered via a separate JSP/container.jsp dynamic call not captured by a direct static fetch.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Legacy JSP architecture with dynamic container.jsp routing makes direct scraping non-trivial; primary content format is PDF (bid results, mine summaries) rather than structured data; no visible API or bulk export.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Legacy JSP e-auction portal with PDF-based results, dynamic container.jsp content routing

accepted_sources.name: MSTC Critical Mineral Block Auction Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape publicly viewable NIT/tender documents and mine block summaries (PDF) pre-login; winning bidder/result data likely requires either post-auction public result PDFs (same pattern as coal block portal) or DSC-gated login for bid-level detail.
accepted_sources.data_available: Real, current auction administration for critical/strategic minerals (lithium, cobalt, rare earths etc.): Notice Inviting Tender, Model Tender Documents, Mine Block Summaries, corrigenda/addenda, bidder query responses, covering an actual First Tranche of 20 blocks launched Nov 2023, with state-level categorization across 15+ states.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch confirmed real auction round data (First Tranche, 20 blocks, Nov 2023) plus registration flows for Bidders/Sellers/Technical Committee. Site migrated Feb 2024 to a version requiring Class-3 Digital Signature Certificates for full access.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Post-Feb-2024 platform requires Class 3 Digital Signature Certificate for transactional access, meaning live bid data during an active auction is inaccessible publicly; only static NIT/tender PDFs and eventual published result PDFs are realistically scrapeable.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Legacy JSP e-auction portal with PDF-based results, DSC-gated transactional access (same family as MSTC Coal Block)

accepted_sources.name: MoSPI PAIMANA (Project Monitoring)
accepted_sources.category: Cost overrun / mega project monitoring database
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape/download monthly PDF Flash Reports and Performance Monitoring Review reports from the public dashboard; parse tabular cost-overrun data per project/ministry; may need to check ipm.mospi.gov.in and cspm.gov.in/english/ocms.html for legacy structured data or APIs
accepted_sources.data_available: Monthly Flash Reports and Performance Monitoring Review reports (PDF) for 1700+ central sector infra projects >=Rs150cr, with cost/schedule slippage data; public dashboard accessible without login; recent publications dated through March 2026
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Public dashboard with Project Monitoring and Performance Monitoring tabs, PDF report downloads under 'What's New', separate sections for high-value project listings; functions primarily as a repository of periodic PDF reports rather than a queryable project-level database in the fetched view
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data appears to be delivered mainly as periodic PDF reports rather than a live searchable database in what was inspected; project-level structured export/API not confirmed — needs deeper crawl of report PDFs to confirm per-project contractor/overrun detail
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF report scraping + OCR/parsing government monitoring portal

accepted_sources.name: NHAI Data Lake 2.0/3.0 GIS Dashboard (PMS)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation to render dashboard and scrape the project table/GIS layer data; inspect underlying XHR/JSON calls feeding the map and table (likely present given dynamic GIS rendering) to pull structured data without full page scraping
accepted_sources.data_available: Structured project table: project name, package, state, district, NH number, length, lanes, project type, mode, capital cost, financial progress %, timeline, PIU/RO contacts; interactive GIS layers including Lok Sabha constituency overlay
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Live GIS dashboard showing NH projects under execution with per-package cost, progress percentage, and constituency mapping; no visible download/export button or documented API in the fetched HTML, but a rich structured table renders directly in the page
accepted_sources.obstacles: No explicit export/API surfaced in the static fetch; likely requires JS execution and network-request inspection to find backing data endpoints; contractor/concessionaire-level detail not confirmed present, only PIU/RO contact info
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Complex browser automation to capture dynamic GIS dashboard JSON

accepted_sources.name: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) India
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct scrape of report listing pages, download and OCR/parse PDF investigation reports for cause findings, operator names, and safety recommendations
accepted_sources.data_available: Hundreds of PDF investigation reports (preliminary and final) for accidents and serious incidents/airprox events, 2012-2026, each with aircraft registration, operator, date, and location
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed real report listings e.g. Pawan Hans AS365N3 VT-PHY near Mayabunder (Feb 2026), Redbird Airways King Air C90A VT-AJV Jharkhand (Feb 2026), Air India A320 VT-ATF Bengaluru serious incident (May 2024), Air India Express B737 VT-AXH Kozhikode (Aug 2020) — active and current through 2026
accepted_sources.obstacles: Reports are PDF-only with narrative text requiring parsing/OCR to extract structured findings; no tabular index confirmed, so building a queryable dataset requires manual/LLM extraction per report
