accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF report scraping + text extraction from government investigation body

accepted_sources.name: PFC Report on Performance of Power Utilities (Annual Integrated Rating)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct PDF download, no auth/JS needed. curl -k succeeds (WebFetch's stricter TLS chain verification fails on this host's cert, but a scraper using standard/relaxed cert handling works fine - site is legitimate and publicly served). Multi-year PDFs can be enumerated via predictable ckfinder path pattern (2015-2025) for a longitudinal per-DISCOM time series; requires PDF table extraction per annexure.
accepted_sources.data_available: Direct PDF archive found at https://www.pfcindia.co.in/ensite/DocumentRepository/ckfinder/files/Operations/Performance_Reports_of_State_Power_Utilities/ with annual reports back to 2020-21. The 2024-25 report (90 pages, 4.7MB) covers 65 of 72 power distribution utilities (42 state DISCOMs, 12 private DISCOMs, 11 power departments), compiled from audited/provisional annual accounts. Contains per-utility annexures: Revenue Details, Revenue/Cost Structure, Profitability and Gap, Cash Adjusted Gap, AT&C losses, billing/collection efficiency, receivables/payables days, net worth, accumulated losses, borrowings.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Extracted real text via pypdf: overall AT&C losses improved from 15.97% (FY23-24) to 15.04% (FY24-25); net worth of distribution utilities negative Rs 1,03,038 crore as of March 2025; accumulated losses Rs 6,47,210 crore; total borrowings Rs 7,26,378 crore. TOC confirms per-utility annexures (Revenue Details pp1-6, Cost Structure pp25-30, Profitability and Gap pp37-42). Report explicitly names DISCOMs that failed to submit accounts (e.g. DNH and DD Power) - itself an accountability signal for flagging non-compliant/opaque utilities.
accepted_sources.obstacles: PDF-only (no CSV/API), tables span multiple pages per annexure and require structured PDF table extraction (headers repeat, columns are utility names). TLS cert chain issue trips strict fetchers - workaround with relaxed cert verification. No single 'all utilities, all years' machine-readable table exists; must stitch across annual PDFs.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF download + table extraction (multi-page annexures, cert-relaxed fetch)

accepted_sources.name: National Power Portal (NPP) India
accepted_sources.category: Power sector centralized data capture system
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: N/A - would require deep dashboard interaction/browser automation to determine if granular data exists beyond aggregates; not confirmed accessible without login for anything beyond generic dashboards
accepted_sources.data_available: GIS-enabled dashboards: Capacity Dashboard (installed capacity by source - nuclear/hydro/thermal/renewable), Generation Dashboard (daily generation by source), Transmission Dashboard (220kV+ network), Coal Status Dashboard (daily stock/receipt/consumption). References separate login-gated subsystems: NPDMS, DRIPS, NIPS.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Landing page confirms dashboard categories exist but content appears to be national/state-level aggregate statistics rather than plant-level or discom-level granularity. No downloadable datasets, CSV exports, or public API documented on the visible landing page. Detailed access likely requires deeper dashboard navigation or authenticated sub-portals (NPDMS/DRIPS/NIPS login walls visible).
accepted_sources.obstacles: Landing page only shows aggregate national/state dashboards; granular (plant/discom-level) data appears gated behind separate authenticated systems (NPDMS, DRIPS, NIPS). No visible public API or bulk export. Essentially duplicates CEA generation statistics already in the platform's integrated source list, without clear additional granularity.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gated dashboard, unconfirmed public data depth

accepted_sources.name: CEA Distribution Policy & Monitoring - UPADHI portal
accepted_sources.category: Consumer grievance data for power sector (MPCSS - Ministry of Power Consumer Service Software)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Would require browser automation (Puppeteer/Playwright) to render JS and inspect network calls for underlying data API - not attempted at this pass since even basic page structure/data existence could not be confirmed
accepted_sources.data_available: Angular single-page application (title 'MPCSS'); no server-rendered content or data visible in raw HTML - all content loads via JS/API calls not captured by static fetch.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Raw HTML is a near-empty Angular shell (22KB, only asset/font links, no body content, title 'MPCSS'). Actual consumer grievance dashboards, if any, are rendered client-side and would require full browser automation (headless Chrome) plus reverse-engineering of underlying API calls to extract data.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Pure client-side rendered SPA with no visible data in source; unknown whether public data views exist without a consumer/complainant login. High implementation cost for uncertain payoff.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: JS-rendered SPA needing browser automation + hidden API discovery

accepted_sources.name: CEA DRIPS Portal (Disaster Resilient Infrastructure for Power Sector)
accepted_sources.category: Disaster resource/vulnerability inventory for power sector
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: N/A - underlying DRIPS portal URL not discoverable from this page; would need further searching to locate the actual system
accepted_sources.data_available: CEA distribution monitoring division page itself is static and links to a PDF announcement ('Launch of the online DRIPS portal') plus SDRF/NDRF norms PDF, but does not directly link to a working public DRIPS data portal or dashboard.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page (107KB) contains links to UPADHI (https://upadhi.cea.gov.in/) and a DRIPS launch announcement PDF, plus SDRF/NDRF fund allocation norms PDF - these are policy/launch documents, not the actual disaster resource inventory dataset itself. No direct link to a functioning DRIPS data portal was found on this page.
accepted_sources.obstacles: The page only announces DRIPS' launch via PDF; the actual portal URL is not linked here. Would need additional search to locate and then likely faces the same JS/auth issues as UPADHI.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: undiscovered portal, policy-document landing page only

accepted_sources.name: PPP in India (DEA) - PPP Project Database (all_infrastructure_projects)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct HTTP GET on the all_infrastructure_projects page returns a large HTML page (3.8MB) with the DataTables-populated table embedded server-side (not purely AJAX-loaded) - can be scraped directly with curl/requests plus HTML table parsing; pagination/sorting is client-side DataTables so full dataset appears to load in one page fetch.
accepted_sources.data_available: DataTables-driven table with real per-project rows: serial number, project name, cost (Rs crore), sector, sub-sector, awarding authority/agency, approval date, state, and project status (Under Construction / Pre-construction Stage / etc). Confirmed ~9,243 numbered table cells present in a single fetch, consistent with thousands of project rows (site claims ~2000 projects >Rs 5 crore; PPPAC alone lists 418 appraised projects worth Rs 1,006,277.73 crore, plus VGF (72 projects, Rs 46,255.96 crore) and IIPDF (31 projects) sub-databases).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Real extracted rows include: '#1: Rs420.00cr, Transport, Ports (excluding captive), V.O.CHIDAMBARANAR PORT TRUST, 31-Mar-2017, Tamil Nadu, Under Construction'; '#3: Storm Water Drainage Scheme (Gurgaon Sector 81-98), Rs253.02cr, Water Sanitation, Haryana Urban Development Authority, 25-Mar-2013, Haryana, Under Construction'. Fields present: project name, cost, sector, sub-sector, awarding authority, approval date, state, status - sufficient granularity to cross-reference award dates/authorities against MCA/court records as originally proposed.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Large single-page payload (3.8MB) requiring HTML table parsing rather than clean API/CSV; concessionaire/private-partner company name field not confirmed present (need deeper column check) - awarding AUTHORITY is government-side, so conflict-of-interest cross-referencing may require an additional per-project detail page to get concessionaire/SPV names.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: server-rendered large HTML table scrape (DataTables)

accepted_sources.name: DoT Gati Shakti Sanchar Portal - Right of Way (RoW) Permissions
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape public pendency/processing-time dashboard pages by state and ministry; monitor per-state policy order PDFs for RoW rule implementation gaps; cross-reference processing-time outliers against telecom operator complaints to expose state-level obstruction patterns.
accepted_sources.data_available: State/UT and ministry-wise pendency dashboards and processing-time statistics for telecom infra (towers, rooftop installations, OFC/fiber) RoW applications; policy implementation orders per state under Telecom RoW Rules 2024; nodal officer contacts; fee structures.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Portal shows real-time application tracking with pendency reports by state/UT and ministry, a six-stage application workflow, and state-specific policy implementation orders dated through mid-2026. Application-level detail requires MeriPehchaan login, but aggregate pendency/processing-time dashboards appear publicly viewable.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Full application-level data (specific applicant, delay reasons) is gated behind MeriPehchaan login; aggregate dashboards may be JS-rendered requiring browser automation; exact dashboard/API endpoint distinct from the landing page needs to be pinned down.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-dashboard-js-rendered-aggregate-stats

accepted_sources.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways - Basic Port Statistics
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Download each year's PDF via the /en/content/basic-port-statistics-<year> pages, extract port-wise cargo/vessel tables via PDF parsing (tabula/pdfplumber), build a 30-year time series per port; cross-reference against Sagarmala project investment tracker and DGCIS (dgciskol.gov.in) coastal/foreign cargo microdata for capacity vs investment mismatches.
accepted_sources.data_available: Annual 'Basic Port Statistics of India' PDF reports spanning 1992-93 through 2024-25 (30+ years), containing port-wise cargo traffic and vessel entry/clearance figures for major Indian ports.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Index page confirmed to link to 10+ discrete annual report entries including 'Basic Port Statistics of India 2024-25', each pointing to a downloadable PDF (e.g. 'BPS 2024-25_compressed.pdf'). The index itself shows no tables directly; actual cargo/vessel metrics are inside each year's PDF, which was not fully retrievable in this pass (400 error on direct PDF fetch) but the page and file existence were confirmed.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data is PDF-only (no CSV/API), requiring PDF table extraction which can be unreliable for older scanned reports; direct PDF URL returned HTTP 400 in this validation pass and must be re-derived via the per-year content page; DGCIS cross-reference source not yet validated.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: gov-pdf-archive-multi-year-tables

accepted_sources.name: Sagarmala Project Tracker (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape rendered HTML table/JS app at sagarmala.gov.in/project/project-tracker (likely needs headless browser due to JS rendering); cross-reference against the static Project Catalogue PDF and periodic PIB status releases for verification; the kaushalbharat.gov.in mirror (sagarmala-report/getproject?state_name=X) may expose a simpler per-state query parameter pattern worth checking for a JSON/API backend.
accepted_sources.data_available: State-wise, sector-wise, and cost-wise breakdown of 845+ Sagarmala port-led infrastructure projects (~Rs 6.06 lakh crore total), including project status (completed/under implementation/under various stages of planning), implementing agency (state govt, NHAI, IWAI, major ports, Indian Railways), category (port modernization, connectivity, coastal community development, industrialization, skill development), and cost figures. A separate PDF Project Catalogue for Investment and a kaushalbharat.gov.in state-filtered project detail view also exist.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Could not render the live tracker table directly (WebFetch failed to parse the JS-driven page content; Chrome browser tool was unavailable in this session). Corroborating web search results and PIB press releases confirm aggregate figures: 315 projects completed (~Rs 1.56 lakh crore), remainder under implementation/planning, broken down by state and sector per official statements.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Page did not render via plain WebFetch (likely client-side JS rendering) and Chrome browser automation was unavailable this session to confirm actual table structure, filters, or export capability. Needs a follow-up pass with a JS-capable fetch to confirm whether project-level (not just aggregate) cost/timeline/contractor data is exposed, and whether committed vs. actual capacity-utilization figures exist to support a genuine 'mismatch' investigative angle.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government infrastructure project tracker: JS-rendered table scrape

accepted_sources.name: CAG Audit Reports Portal (SAI India)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape audit-report listing pages per state AG office (sector/year filters visible in URL params e.g. ?sector[0]=27&page=2), then download and OCR/parse linked PDFs for department-level findings, financial irregularities, and PSU governance issues. Cross-reference report metadata (state, year, sector) against MyNeta legislator records and MPLADS data already integrated.
accepted_sources.data_available: Full-text CAG audit reports (Performance, Compliance, Revenue, Commercial/PSU, State Finances) as PDFs, organized by state Accountant General office, sector, and report number/year. Confirmed active with 2025/2026 reports (e.g. 'Report No. 1 of 2025' on State Finances 2023-24, Report No. 2 of 2025 on State Bank of Sikkim performance audit, Report No. 5/6 of 2025 Compliance/Performance Audit Civil).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Search-confirmed direct download URLs like cag.gov.in/webroot/uploads/download_audit_report/2025/... show specific, recent (2025-2026) reports with granular titles, e.g. state finances audits, performance audit of Delhi public health infrastructure 2016-17 to 2021-22, and PSU-specific compliance audits. State-level sub-portals exist (e.g. cag.gov.in/ag1/kerala/en/audit-report). Direct WebFetch to the root page timed out (socket hang up) likely due to bot-blocking/heavy JS, but content is verifiably real and current via search-indexed pages and direct PDF links.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Direct automated fetch may hit bot protection/timeouts (observed socket hang up on root page); reports are PDF-only requiring text extraction; site has fragmented state-wise sub-domains (cag.gov.in/ag1/<state>) needing separate crawl logic; some reports are pre-OCR scanned images requiring OCR.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF scraping + state sub-portal crawl

accepted_sources.name: AuditOnline (Ministry of Panchayati Raj)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Use the public citizen section (no login required for aggregate/observation data) with state -> district (ZP) -> block (BP) -> village (GP) drill-down and fiscal year selectors; scrape observation/KPI tables. Full audit reports/settlement details likely require registered auditor/auditee login, so acquisition is limited to public aggregate + observation-level data unless a public report-download endpoint is found during implementation.
accepted_sources.data_available: Panchayati Raj Institution (PRI) audit tracking across Zilla Panchayat (district), Block Panchayat, and Gram Panchayat (village) levels, with a public citizen-facing section showing audit scheduling, audit team composition, observation analysis, KPI reports, and consolidated year-end summaries. Fiscal year filter available 2019-2020 through 2025-2026.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed via fetch (on the non-www variant; www subdomain has a certificate mismatch error): public section lists counts of enlisted auditors/auditees, audit plans prepared, observations recorded, generated audit reports, and settlement/action-taken reports, filterable hierarchically by ZP/BP/GP and fiscal year. This is genuinely novel and largely uncovered ground — local government fund misuse at village/block level rarely appears in national press.
accepted_sources.obstacles: SSL certificate mismatch on www.auditonline.gov.in (must use bare auditonline.gov.in); most detailed data behind username/password/CAPTCHA login; public section appears to expose only aggregate counts and observation summaries, not full audit narrative text; state-wise drill-down navigation likely JS-heavy requiring browser automation.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: authenticated/gated portal with public aggregate drill-down

accepted_sources.name: RBI State Finances: A Study of Budgets
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct download of per-year Excel statement files and the consolidated e-STATES database archive; build a longitudinal state-fiscal-indicator dataset (2002-2026) to flag anomalous spending/revenue/deficit spikes correlated with election years or specific administrations, then cross-reference against MyNeta candidate/MP-MLA data and MPLADS.
accepted_sources.data_available: Annual RBI publication 'State Finances: A Study of Budgets' with 37 detailed statements and 4 appendices per edition covering deficit indicators, revenue receipts/expenditures, capital transactions, development vs non-development spending, interest payments, tax revenues, market borrowings, outstanding liabilities, and social sector (education/health/sanitation) spending, disaggregated by state. Historical archive from 2002 to the 2025-26 edition (released Jan 2026).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed via direct fetch: latest edition is 'State Finances: A Study of Budgets of 2025-26' (released Jan 23, 2026), with PDF chapters/statements/appendices plus Excel spreadsheets for each data table, and a consolidated 15.2MB 'e-STATES' database bundling all state-level financial data across years. This is genuinely machine-readable (Excel) and independently produced by RBI (not self-reported by states), making it strong for cross-checking state government fiscal claims.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Page requires navigating ASPX postback-style year archive links; Excel files are per-statement (37+ files per year) requiring assembly into a unified longitudinal dataset; older years (pre-2015) may only have PDF, not Excel.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: structured government publication archive (PDF/Excel download)

accepted_sources.name: CGA Union Government Monthly Accounts Dashboard
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Download published monthly .xlsm files directly and parse with openpyxl/pandas. No auth or heavy JS rendering needed for the file itself.
accepted_sources.data_available: Downloadable monthly .xlsm Excel dashboard covering Total Receipts, Total Expenditure, and Deficit components since April 2015, updated monthly (latest: Feb 2026), with Budget/Revised Estimate comparisons and YoY growth breakdowns.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page confirms an interactive dashboard with selectable financial year/month, 5-year comparative components, and a downloadable Excel file link; actual raw table not visible without downloading the .xlsm.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Actual figures live only inside the downloadable Excel, not the HTML page — requires locating/mapping each month's .xlsm URL rather than a single stable API endpoint.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government Excel/PDF report portal — download and parse periodic files

accepted_sources.name: India Budget - Expenditure Profile & Demands for Grants (allsbe.pdf)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct HTTPS download of the PDF (curl with a browser User-Agent works; default WebFetch was blocked with 403, likely bot-protection on some UAs). Parse with pdftotext/pdfplumber to extract the ministry-wise tables; combine with per-demand detail PDFs for scheme-level granularity.
accepted_sources.data_available: 7.2MB PDF, Expenditure Budget 2026-2027 with Notes on Demands for Grants — ministry/department-wise Budget Estimates split into Revenue, Capital and Total (Rs crores), with page references into detailed demand-wise volumes.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Verified via pdftotext extraction: table lists every Ministry/Department (Agriculture, Atomic Energy, Ayush, Chemicals & Fertilisers, Civil Aviation, Coal, Commerce, Communications, Consumer Affairs, Cooperation, etc.) with exact BE 2026-27 figures, e.g. MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION: Revenue 12677.46, Capital 45.00, Total 17843.90 crore, with page ranges 30-32 into the detailed demands volume.
accepted_sources.obstacles: WebFetch tool returned 403 (bot blocking on default UA) — required curl with a browser User-Agent header to succeed. Document is large (7MB) and requires PDF table parsing, not machine-readable out of the box.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government Excel/PDF report portal — download and parse periodic files

accepted_sources.name: GST Portal Statistics Download
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct download of .xlsx files per year/category; parse with pandas/openpyxl. Static links, no login required for the statistics section.
accepted_sources.data_available: Extensive downloadable .xlsx files by financial year (2017-18 through 2026-27): active taxpayer registration counts by state, GSTR-3B tax liability, GSTR-1 outward supply details, gross/net tax collection by state, IGST settlements, and E-way Bill statistics from 2018-19 onward. Also an 8-year GST statistical report PDF.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Page organizes download links by financial year and data category (Registration, GSTR-3B, GSTR-1, Collections, IGST Settlement, E-way Bill), all in .xlsx format, spanning 9+ fiscal years — confirmed real structured downloadable statistics, not just narrative text.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Files split across many separate year/category links requiring a scraper to enumerate all download URLs; some categories only available from certain years onward (e.g. E-way Bill from 2018-19).
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government Excel/PDF report portal — download and parse periodic files

accepted_sources.name: DIPAM Disinvestment Receipts
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: HTML table scrape per financial year (dropdown-driven, likely simple GET/POST per year parameter); no auth required.
accepted_sources.data_available: Year-wise (FY2015-16 through FY2026-27, selectable via dropdown) table of CPSE disinvestment transactions: % of GoI shares disinvested, method (OFS/strategic sale/etc.), receipts in Rs crore, and post-disinvestment GoI shareholding.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Verified live table for FY2026-27 with real entries: Central Bank of India 8.08% via OFS raising Rs 2,266.13 crore; Coal India Ltd 2.0% via OFS raising Rs 5,542.36 crore; NHPC Limited 6.01% via OFS raising Rs 4,357.36 crore. Also notes on special cases (NINL enterprise value Rs 12,100 crore, FSNL Rs 320 crore).
accepted_sources.obstacles: Table is rendered per selected year via dropdown, so a scraper must iterate each FY value; no bulk CSV/API export currently observed on the page itself.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State/regulatory HTML data table with year-selector — iterate and scrape

accepted_sources.name: Public Enterprises Survey (PE Survey Reports)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct download of per-year Statement*.xlsx and NMDS master Excel files from the year-specific subpage (found by following homepage/pesurveyreports_current.asp and homepage/pesurveyreportsfy{year}.asp links); parse xlsx with pandas/openpyxl.
accepted_sources.data_available: Annual Dept. of Public Enterprises Survey reports (e.g. FY2024-25) with full English/Hindi PDF reports plus 9 separate Statement PDFs and matching .xlsx files (Statement1.xlsx through Statement9.xlsx) containing CPSE-wise financial data (profit/loss, net worth, investment, employment) plus an NMDS (National CPSE) master dataset Excel file.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed via subpage homepage/pesurveyreportsfy2024-25.asp: real download links for PESurveyReportFY2024-25_English.pdf, PESurveyReportFY2024-25_Hindi.pdf, NMDS_for_PE_Survey_2024_25_Department_of_Public_Enterprises.xlsx, and Statement 1-9 (both PDF and matching xlsx pairs, e.g. Statement 1/STATEMENT A, Statement 3/STATEMENT B) — a structured, per-CPSE financial dataset covering profit/loss, employment, investment.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Initial WebFetch attempts failed with 'unable to verify the first certificate' (TLS cert issue on the default fetch client); required curl with -k (or a scraper with proper CA bundle) plus browser UA. Root URL redirects through homepage/homepage.asp then needs following year-specific subpages to reach actual file links — not a single flat file list.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government Excel/PDF report portal — download and parse periodic files

accepted_sources.name: 16th Finance Commission Report Data (PRS India Summary)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Fetch PRS summary page (HTML/markdown) for table data; download linked official PDF for full commission report and cross-reference against actual Union Budget transfer data (already-integrated MPLADS/Sansad sources) to detect shortfalls in promised vs actual devolution to specific states.
accepted_sources.data_available: PRS summary of the 16th Finance Commission report (tabled Feb 2026), containing 5 tables: tax distribution criteria/weightages, grants-in-aid breakdown (Rs 9.47 lakh crore), state-wise shares across 14th/15th/16th FC for comparison, list of 23 eligible cities for infrastructure grants, and state-wise grant allocations in Rs crore. Downloadable PDF summary linked.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed real tabular content: Table 3 compares individual state shares across three Finance Commissions (14th/15th/16th), Table 5 gives state-wise grant allocations in Rs crore by category. Freshly relevant since report was tabled Feb 1, 2026, enabling checks of whether actual devolution/transfers to states match Commission recommendations.
accepted_sources.obstacles: PRS is a secondary summary, not the primary source - for rigorous investigative use should be cross-checked against the official Finance Commission report PDF (finance ministry site) for exact figures. No access obstacles; page is fully public and fetched successfully.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF/table scraping of a policy summary page plus linked official PDF report

accepted_sources.name: ONDLS - Online National Drug Licensing System (State Drugs Control)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Individual license-number lookups via public verification tool (no bulk export found); would require systematic querying across license number ranges or scraping search results per state/district for the pharmacy locator to build any aggregate dataset - no bulk download or API discovered.
accepted_sources.data_available: Centralized CDAC/CDSCO-built portal for drug/cosmetics licensing with a public License Verification tool (search by license number) and a Pharmacy/Blood Center Locator (by state/district/pincode). Reference materials (application forms 19-36, license forms 20-37, Drugs & Cosmetics Act text) also available.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage loaded but all statistics counters (active licenses, approved applications, registered firms, technical persons) showed 0, suggesting either a fresh/broken deployment or that real data sits behind search-only interfaces not visible on landing page. A guessed /statistics endpoint returned 404, indicating no public aggregate/bulk statistics page exists.

Dashboard counters showing zero raise doubt about whether the aggregation layer is populated at all. Would require record-by-record scraping via the verification search, which is high effort for uncertain payoff.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: record-by-record government portal lookup with no bulk API

accepted_sources.name: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) National Health Providers Registry (NHPR, formerly HFR search)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires headless browser automation to render the SPA and either scrape rendered table rows or discover the underlying JSON search API the frontend calls (network tab inspection needed).
accepted_sources.data_available: Searchable registry of registered health facilities (hospitals, clinics, diagnostic labs, imaging centers, pharmacies), public+private, with unique HFR ID, ownership type, address, and verification status.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch confirmed the originally-flagged URL (facility.abdm.gov.in/searchV2) 301-redirects to nhpr.abdm.gov.in, titled 'NHPR ABDM - National Healthcare Providers Registry', confirming the registry is live under a renamed domain. Page is a client-rendered SPA so no table rows were extractable via static fetch; the dashboard.abdm.gov.in/abdm/ companion stats page returned only a bare 'ABDM-Insights' title with no visible data via WebFetch, likely also JS-rendered.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Original URL (facility.abdm.gov.in/searchV2) has been silently renamed/redirected to nhpr.abdm.gov.in as of 2026 - update bookmarks. Client-side rendering blocks static/WebFetch scraping entirely; no browser automation tool was available in this session to confirm actual data fields or record counts, so acceptance is based on redirect + title metadata only, not verified content.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: JS-rendered SPA with hidden REST API, needs browser automation to discover endpoint

accepted_sources.name: CTRI - Clinical Trials Registry India (Advanced Search)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Web form scraping (POST-based search) plus per-trial detail page scraping; no public bulk API but structure is stable and has been scraped by academic researchers before.
accepted_sources.data_available: Nationally mandatory prospective clinical trial registry (since 2009) with fielded search by trial status, type, registration period (2007-2026), study category, study design, phase, primary sponsor, recruitment status, state/district, and free-text keyword. Individual trial records include sponsor, investigator, sites, phase, intervention, and (where available) results/publication status.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Search form confirmed live with real fielded filters (sponsor category, phase 1-4, recruitment status, state/district, keyword). Academic literature (PMC) confirms researchers already use CTRI systematically to study registration completeness and result-reporting gaps, including a cited finding that ~12% of regulatory trials go unregistered.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No bulk download/API; requires scraping search results and paginating per-trial detail pages. Cross-referencing against CDSCO drug approval data (separate portal) needed to complete the investigative angle.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government trial registry scraper (form POST + detail-page HTML parse)

accepted_sources.name: FSSAI FoSCoS Food Recall Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Web form scraping of recall search interface; likely POST-based with paginated results per license/category/year.

Every recall (FBO-initiated or authority-directed) gets a unique traceable case ID with progressing status.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed via secondary source (Outlook Business, FSSAI site) that this is a real, newly launched (March 2026) structured recall system replacing the old fragmented manual/PDF notice process, with filters for license number, product, category, financial year.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Domain is food safety, not strictly health, though has direct public-health linkage (contamination, outbreaks). accepted_sources.name: CBSE OSM (On-Screen Marking) 2026 Results Scandal — vendor Coempt Edu Teck
accepted_sources.category: Education board results anomalies / vendor procurement accountability
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Manual article scraping plus follow-up CPPP tender-record pull for Coempt Edu Teck's bid history and RTI to CBSE for vendor due-diligence records
accepted_sources.confidence: Medium — strong narrative lead with concrete procurement angle, but core investigative payoff depends on accessing CPPP records which is a known-difficult source
accepted_sources.data_available: Investigative news reporting with granular figures: 40 crore scanned pages, 98,66,622 answer books, pass % dropped to 85.20% (7-yr low), vendor procurement history (RFP dated Aug 28 2025, Coempt Edu Teck vs TCS bid). Underlying primary data (CPPP tender/bid documents) would need separate lookup — article itself is narrative journalism, not raw data.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Article documents CBSE's 2026 Class 12 OSM rollout failure: wrong/illegible/missing answer sheets, portal crashes, and a vendor-selection process that awarded the contract to Coempt Edu Teck (formerly Globarena Technologies) despite its track record of two prior Telangana exam-system failures (2019, 2023) linked to reported student suicides. No mention of the claimed master-password/AWS-bucket security breach was found in this specific article; that detail was not verifiable from this source alone.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Single news article, not a structured dataset. Deep investigation requires cross-referencing CPPP tender IDs (CPPP is a previously attempted-and-failed source per project brief — would need a new angle/approach) and Telangana government exam-authority records for the 2019/2023 precedents. Security-breach claim (master password, AWS bucket) needs independent verification from another source before use.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: News-article monitoring + government tender-record cross-reference

accepted_sources.name: 2026 NEET-UG Controversy / CBI investigation
accepted_sources.category: Education entrance-exam integrity / law enforcement investigation records

accepted_sources.confidence: Medium — good entity-extraction seed but not itself a novel data source; value is primarily as a bridge to already-integrated Indian Kanoon/CBI sources
accepted_sources.data_available: Wikipedia summary article with structured facts: 2.27M candidates affected, ~120-140 question overlap identified, 13+ arrests by CBI (names, roles listed: coaching owner, professors, NTA subject expert, physics/biology teachers, a pediatrician), re-exam date June 21 2026, evidence types (electronic devices, financial records, WhatsApp chats). Underlying primary source would be CBI chargesheets/court filings on Indian Kanoon (already integrated) once filed.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirms NEET-UG 2026 exam (2.27M candidates) was cancelled after a leaked guess paper matched the real paper; CBI arrested over a dozen people including an NTA-appointed subject expert, revealing links to the same syndicate behind the 2024 NEET leak across Rajasthan/Maharashtra. Includes named individuals and arrest details, useful as an entity list for cross-referencing with Indian Kanoon court records.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Wikipedia itself is a secondary/tertiary source and will require continual updates as the case develops; the actual investigative depth comes from court filings not yet fully public. Overlaps with already-integrated Indian Kanoon and CBI press release sources rather than being a wholly new acquisition pipeline.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Wikipedia/wiki-style structured page scraping

accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Once backend stabilizes, scrape MAITRI/ecmpcb.in granted-consent search results by industry name/district; may need to enumerate via form POST or discover updated URL paths (old ecmpcb.in paths appear stale/404).

Backend search/application system is the MAITRI portal and ec-MPCB (ecmpcb.in).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: The mpcb.gov.in procedure page is informational only (describes CTE/CTO application workflow) and does not itself expose a searchable database; it points to ecmpcb.in and the MAITRI portal, which advertise 'Granted Consent', 'Granted EC', and SEIAA/SEAC notification search features. Direct attempt to reach ecmpcb.in's GrantedConsent page returned HTTP 404, and the bare domain returned HTTP 503 on a raw curl check, indicating the backend is currently unstable or the specific search path has changed.
accepted_sources.obstacles: ecmpcb.in backend returned 404 on the expected GrantedConsent.aspx path and 503 on the bare domain — the portal may have migrated to MAITRI (maitri.mahaonline.gov.in) entirely; need to find current working search endpoint. Also likely session-cookie/viewstate (ASP.NET) driven.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state-gov-dynamic-portal-with-search-forms

accepted_sources.name: Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape OCEMS dashboard for real-time emissions data by industry; scrape downloadable AAQ/water quality datasets; cross-reference SEIAA Gujarat clearance portal separately for project-level environmental clearance orders tied to specific companies.
accepted_sources.data_available: Air and water quality monitoring data (downloadable), hazardous waste facility/authorized-user lists, industry categorization, OCEMS (Online Continuous Emissions Monitoring System) public dashboard, and links to Parivesh (environmental clearance tracking), SEIAA Gujarat, and GCZMA (coastal zone) portals.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage confirms the board publishes downloadable ambient air/water quality datasets and operates an OCEMS public dashboard for continuous emissions monitoring, plus links out to SEIAA/GCZMA clearance portals. No single unified public search across all consent/CTE-CTO records was found on the homepage; consent records appear to require navigating to sub-portals or contacting regional offices.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No unified consent search found on homepage; likely need to locate specific sub-portal (XGN online consent system mentioned in original brief was not directly verified) and OCEMS dashboard may require JS rendering for live data.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state-gov-dynamic-portal-with-search-forms

accepted_sources.name: GIDC (Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation) Estate/Allotment Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape egov.gidcgujarat.org LandEstateDetails.aspx for plot-level allotment records across estates; cross-reference GIS map layer for spatial allotment patterns; look for OCA letter download endpoints that may reveal allottee company names.
accepted_sources.data_available: Plot/shed availability and allotment details across 239 industrial estates in Gujarat, via the e-governance sub-portal egov.gidcgujarat.org/gidcgg/LandEstateDetails.aspx, including OCA (Offer-Cum-Allotment) letters, plot pricing, and GIS estate mapping.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live portal describing a public 'Available Plot/Shed Details' search and GIS mapping tool for all 239 estates, plus fraud warnings about unauthorized intermediaries -- signaling this is an actively monitored, higher-stakes allotment process worth scrutiny. Actual allotment recipient (company-level) data was not directly sampled from the sub-portal in this pass.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Sub-portal (egov.gidcgujarat.org) not directly verified this session; likely ASP.NET WebForms with viewstate/postback pagination per estate, requiring per-estate iteration; allottee identity fields may be redacted or require deeper drill-down per plot.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: state-gov-dynamic-portal-with-search-forms

accepted_sources.name: MP e-Procurement Portal (MPTenders)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Structured HTML scraping of tender listing/search pages and corrigendum feed (NIC nicgep platform, same family as other state NIC eProcurement portals); pagination + POST-based search forms.
accepted_sources.data_available: Live tender listings (10+ active tenders on homepage) with department/organization, closing dates, location, tender value class; corrigenda updated every 15 minutes; archive/tender-status tracking; cancelled/retendered records; nodal officer directory.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Homepage listed active tenders spanning MP departments (e.g. construction in Vidisha, power plant equipment procurement) with closing dates in Jul-Aug 2026, searchable by closing date/location/organization/classification. Standard NIC nicgep e-Procurement platform.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Standard NIC eProcurement session/CSRF handling for deep search; per-tender drill-down needed for award/L1 bidder data; historical archive depth unverified.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: NIC eProcurement (nicgep) tender portal scraper

accepted_sources.name: Chhattisgarh eProcurement Portal (CHIPS/CHEPS)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Follow meta-refresh redirect to CHEPS getSignInAction.do, then scrape tender search/listing endpoints; likely needs headless browser due to JS-rendered listings and CSRF tokens rotating per session.
accepted_sources.data_available: CHEPS e-Tendering System (IBM WebSphere-based) live tender/bid listings, sign-in and tender search actions, CSRF-token protected pages, department/board/corporation/municipal body tenders for CG state.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Raw HTML retrieval confirmed a functioning, actively served CHEPS e-Tendering System redirecting to getSignInAction.do with OWASP CSRF tokens on all asset URLs; homepage is a client-side redirect/loading shell so listing content requires following the redirect chain and rendering JS-driven search forms.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Homepage is JS/meta-refresh loading shell; requires session handling and CSRF token capture; deeper award data likely needs login or multi-step navigation.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: CHIPS/CHEPS e-Tendering portal scraper (IBM WebSphere, distinct from NIC nicgep family)

accepted_sources.name: Madhya Pradesh Directorate of Local Fund Audit (LFA)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Download and parse PDF audit reports per regional office/year; scrape lists of audited bodies and embezzlement case pages; likely needs OCR for older scanned reports.
accepted_sources.data_available: Consolidated annual audit reports for panchayati raj institutions (2013-14 through 2021-22) and urban local body reports, MP Local Fund Audit Act 1973 text and rules, audit manuals, lists of audited bodies, embezzlement case details, workload/computerization reports, SAS exam results.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Portal (Hindi/English) hosts downloadable multi-year consolidated audit reports for panchayats and urban bodies, an embezzlement-cases section, and lists of audited institutions across 7 regional offices (Bhopal, Indore, Jabalpur, etc.) -- a genuinely under-scrutinized municipal financial irregularity dataset distinct from CAG.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Reports are PDF (some likely scanned/non-machine-readable for older years); site structure appears to require per-region/per-year navigation; primarily Hindi-language content needing translation for full-text search.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State audit body PDF report harvester (regional office + year-based navigation)

accepted_sources.name: Chhattisgarh Bhuiyan Land Records
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Query khasra/village-wise search forms (likely POST with district/tehsil/village dropdowns) to extract parcel and revenue-court-case data at scale; combine with Bhunaksha map layer for spatial cross-referencing of land disputes in mining-affected tribal districts.
accepted_sources.data_available: Khasra parcel details, B1/P-II certificate generation, aggregated statistics (~25.4 million total land parcels, 2.9 million government-owned), revenue court case tracking, crop-wise coverage reports, separate admin logins for Bhunaksha maps and girdawari field-survey data.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Official Revenue and Disaster Management Department portal exposing khasra search, B1/PII digitally-signed certificate retrieval, revenue court case module, and aggregate statewide land-parcel statistics; distinct modules for maps (Bhunaksha) and field survey (girdawari) requiring separate access.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Multi-step cascading dropdown navigation (district->tehsil->village->khasra); revenue court case data may be siloed in separate module with its own auth; large-scale scraping likely rate-limited given 25M+ parcel records.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State Bhulekh/Bhuiyan land-record cascading-dropdown scraper

accepted_sources.name: Assam ILRMS / Dharitree Land Records Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Per-village lookup scraping via district/circle/village dropdowns feeding jamabandi and Bhunaksha queries; likely requires session/form-post handling
accepted_sources.data_available: Jamabandi (Records of Rights) copies with transliteration, legacy property registration records, Bhunaksha cadastral mapping, NOC/objection-petition filings for property transfer, Mission Basundhara and NGDRS registration services
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched successfully. Portal confirmed as the correct URL (revenueassam.nic.in and dharitree.assam.gov.in are both unreachable/wrong; ilrms.assam.gov.in is the live, correct entry point). Offers jamabandi viewing, cadastral maps via Bhunaksha, and legacy registration record search, with separate citizen vs official (Dharitree) access tiers.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Exact query parameters and drill-down hierarchy not fully visible from homepage; some officer-only functions (Dharitree proper) may be access-gated separately from citizen ILRMS front end; bulk/systematic scraping across all villages likely to hit rate limits or CAPTCHAs
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Multi-step form-driven govt record lookup (district->circle->village->plot), session/state handling required

accepted_sources.name: Odisha Forest Land Information Decision Support System (FLI-DSS)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Attempt public report generation via any open AOI-query tool on the site; if gated, pursue RTI request for FLI-DSS-generated project clearance overlap reports, or cross-reference via Parivesh (MoEFCC portal) forest clearance case files which often cite FLI-DSS outputs
accepted_sources.data_available: GIS-based reports on notified/revenue forest, diverted forest lands, protected areas, sanctuaries, wildlife corridors, and eco-sensitive zones; generates area-of-interest reports on forest/ESZ/national park/sanctuary boundary involvement for proposed projects, using Survey of India, Forest Survey of India, and satellite imagery layers
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched successfully. Site is real and describes report-generation capability for forest diversion overlap analysis, a genuinely useful tool for checking whether mining/industrial project sites encroach protected areas. However the homepage is login-gated and does not clearly expose which report functions are public vs restricted; only a downloadable user manual is confirmed public.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Login requirement likely blocks self-service report generation for arbitrary coordinates; unclear if any public-facing query tool exists versus purely internal admin use
accepted_sources.implementation_family: GIS decision-support portal, login-gated report generation, RTI/cross-reference fallback

accepted_sources.name: Odisha Forestry GIS / OFMS (Forest Management System)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Directory/path enumeration of odishaforestgis.in/ofms/uploads/ for individual district PDF reports (CA Landbank lists etc.) that are apparently linked/indexed without requiring login; supplement with RTI for patrolling/fire/plantation logs behind the login wall
accepted_sources.data_available: Intended to track patrolling, plantation activity, and forest-fire monitoring per the source description; homepage itself is purely a login screen
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched successfully but returned only a login page with no visible public data, reports, or downloadable content. A related public PDF was found via search (odishaforestgis.in/ofms/uploads/drfl/angul2222.pdf, a CA Landbank list for Angul district in degraded revenue forests), suggesting some uploaded documents under /uploads/ may be directly linkable/discoverable even though the main app is gated.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Core monitoring dashboards (patrolling, fire, plantation) are behind login; only incidentally-indexed uploaded PDFs appear accessible without credentials; systematic access requires either credentials or RTI request
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Login-gated monitoring dashboard with an apparently open /uploads/ document directory, RTI fallback for restricted data

accepted_sources.name: Assam Online Consent Management & Monitoring System (OCMMS) - Pollution Control Board
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape the granted/rejected/pending application search results (likely paginated, possibly POST-based search forms by industry name/district/date range)
accepted_sources.data_available: Public-facing searchable databases: Consent Applications Under Process, Consent Granted Applications (CTE/CTO), Consent Rejected Applications, Waste Management Granted Applications; downloadable SOPs/guidance for e-waste, plastic waste, battery waste compliance
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched successfully. Confirmed as a live, publicly searchable regulatory consent database covering approved, pending, and rejected industrial pollution consents across Assam, including a distinct hazardous/waste-management consent category — directly useful for cross-referencing industries (tea, oil/ONGC/OIL, coal) against compliance status.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Search forms likely require specific query parameters (industry type, district, date range) rather than offering full bulk listing; pagination and possible CAPTCHA on repeated queries
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Public regulatory consent search portal, paginated/POST search forms

accepted_sources.name: West Bengal Online Consent Management & Monitoring System (WBOCMMS) - WBPCB
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape granted/rejected application search results on WBOCMMS for historical data (pre-2023); separately investigate Silpa Sathi Portal for current live consent data
accepted_sources.data_available: Consent Pending, Under Scrutiny, Granted, and Rejected Applications; Granted Waste Management applications; general industry details database
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched successfully. Confirms same architecture as Assam's OCMMS sibling system, tracking CTE/CTO applications through their lifecycle. Notably, since Jan 1 2023 new applications route through the separate 'Silpa Sathi Portal', meaning WBOCMMS may now mostly hold pre-2023 historical records rather than current live applications — still valuable for a historical baseline of industrial clusters like Haldia/Durgapur.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Post-Jan-2023 data likely migrated to Silpa Sathi Portal (not yet validated), meaning WBOCMMS alone gives an incomplete/dated picture; search form parameters and pagination behavior not yet tested
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Public regulatory consent search portal, paginated/POST search forms (same family as Assam OCMMS)

accepted_sources.name: CAG Local Body Audit Reports - Odisha (AG-Odisha, PAG Audit-II)
accepted_sources.category: Audit / State Finances, Performance, Compliance, IT audits with Local Body/Panchayat Raj/Urban Local Body filters
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape paginated HTML listing (9 pages) for report metadata and PDF links; apply Local Bodies/PRI/ULB filter; download and OCR/parse PDFs for scheme-specific findings (e.g., pension fund misappropriation, EPF non-remittance) at district/PRI level.
accepted_sources.data_available: 89 total downloadable PDF audit reports, paginated (10/page), filterable by Local Bodies / Panchayat Raj Institutions / Urban Local Bodies / sector. Recent examples: Report on State Finances for the year 2024-25 (31 Mar 2026, 7.24MB), Report on School Education in the State (09 Dec 2025), IT audits on CCTNS and e-Procurement System (24 Sep 2025), Performance Audit of POSHAN and Mid-Day Meal, Management of Odisha Mineral Bearing Areas Development Corporation Funds.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live, paginated list of 89 downloadable PDF audit reports with dates/titles/sizes; explicit Local Bodies/PRI/ULB filter categories exist though the sample page shown skewed toward state-level reports rather than local-body misappropriation cases specifically.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Reports are PDFs requiring parsing/OCR for structured extraction; local-body-specific misappropriation findings are buried within larger sector reports rather than a standalone dataset, requiring full-text mining across the 89 reports to surface specific cases.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: cag_audit_report_scraper

accepted_sources.name: CAG Audit Reports - Bihar (Accountant General Bihar)
accepted_sources.category: Audit / State finance and scheme-specific compliance/performance audits
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape the same cag.gov.in AG-state template used across states; filter to Local Bodies/scheme-specific performance audits; download and parse PDFs for compliance para extraction (e.g., MGNREGA, health scheme irregularities).
accepted_sources.data_available: Chronological list of downloadable PDF audit reports back to 2002, filterable by government type (Union/State/Local Bodies), sector, report category. Examples: Report No. 4 of 2025 - Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY performance audit; Report No. 1 of 2025 - State Finances Audit Report (year ended Mar 2024); Performance Audit on Public Health Infrastructure and Management of Health Services (Nov 2024); Compliance audit for year ended March 2022.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live listing with real, dated, titled PDF reports including scheme-specific performance audits (health, PMJAY) and a Local Bodies filter category, giving a re-attempt angle distinct from the previously rejected generic national CAG portal.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Same PDF parsing burden as other CAG state portals; scheme-specific findings require reading full report bodies, not just listing metadata; site structure is identical to the already-rejected national CAG entry, so distinctiveness rests entirely on state/local-body filtering.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: cag_audit_report_scraper

accepted_sources.name: Jharkhand Legislative Assembly - National eVidhan Application (NeVA)
accepted_sources.category: Legislative accountability records / state assembly questions and proceedings
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape/paginate the questions-and-answers module (likely POST-based search with session filters) for MLA-wise and topic-wise questions; cross-reference with mining/tribal welfare keywords; NeVA is a shared platform used by multiple state assemblies so the scraper pattern may be reusable.
accepted_sources.data_available: Starred/unstarred assembly questions and ministerial answers, bills, committee reports, session calendar, governor's address, member directory (81 members). Homepage shows aggregate counts: 882 notices, 848 questions, 6 government bills, 70 documents laid.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Publicly viewable without login (login is a separate optional feature); site is a live, actively updated NeVA instance with substantive counts of questions/answers/bills that can be mined for ministerial admissions on mining, tribal welfare, and corruption topics raised on the floor.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Bilingual (Hindi/English) content complicates keyword search; NeVA platforms often use dynamic JS-rendered search forms and session tokens requiring browser automation rather than simple HTTP scraping; content depth (full answer text vs. just question titles) not yet verified.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: neva_state_assembly_scraper

accepted_sources.name: Odisha eProcurement Portal (tendersodisha.gov.in)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape the NIC-GEP standard listing pages for active tenders/results/debarment lists; cross-reference winning bidder names across tenders and departments over time to detect repeat-winner or bid-rigging patterns; note NIC-GEP is used by many state governments so acquisition pattern is reusable.
accepted_sources.data_available: Publicly searchable active tenders (titles, reference numbers, closing/bid-opening dates, corrigendums), tender results, cancelled/retendered tenders, debarment lists, browse by organisation/location/classification/closing date, MIS reports dashboard, updates every 15 minutes.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live NIC-GEP (National Informatics Centre Government e-Procurement) portal with no-login public access to active tenders, results, and a debarment list, giving distinct state-level data structure from the already-rejected central CPPP portal for bid-rigging/vendor pattern analysis.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Detailed bidder-level information requires login; site likely uses ASP.NET viewstate/postback forms typical of NIC-GEP deployments, complicating simple scraping and requiring session/cookie handling; tender document PDFs need separate parsing.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: nicgep_state_eprocurement_scraper

accepted_sources.name: Rajasthan State Information Commission (RIC) - RTI Appeal/Complaint Decisions
accepted_sources.category: State Government Portals - North (Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan, HP, J&K, Uttarakhand)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape decision list pages (HTML tables) then download/OCR linked PDFs for decision text (department, PIO, complainant issue, ruling). Multi-step: crawl each decision category page, paginate, fetch PDFs, extract text via PDF parsing/OCR since some may be scanned.
accepted_sources.data_available: RTI second-appeal and complaint decisions (PIO refusals, delays), Remarkable Appeal/Complaint Decisions, Supreme Court and High Court RTI-related rulings, circulars/notices — spanning years of RTI enforcement actions against Rajasthan public authorities.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Circulars.aspx confirmed as a working HTML table (S.No./Title/View) linking to PDF orders (e.g. writereaddata/Circulars/... .pdf). WebPolicy.aspx confirms dedicated menu sections: Decision of Appeals, Decision of Complaints, Decision of Online Appeals/Complaints, Remarkable Appeal Decisions, Remarkable Complaint Decisions, High Court Decisions. This is a live RTI appellate body archive — decisions name the public authority/department that denied information, which is directly useful for tracking which departments obstruct transparency.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Decision PDFs appear scan-quality in places (title showed as garbled 'Munesh Ji Catetaker' in one fetch, suggesting inconsistent OCR/metadata); no visible search/filter API; no pagination info confirmed, may require ASPX postback handling (viewstate) for browsing which complicates simple scraping.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: ASPX government portal with PDF-based decision archive; needs viewstate-aware scraping + PDF text extraction/OCR pipeline

accepted_sources.name: RAJKAJ Integrated e-Office - Circulars & Orders
accepted_sources.category: State Government Portals - North (Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan, HP, J&K, Uttarakhand)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Static HTML scrape of the single list page, download linked PDFs for full circular text.
accepted_sources.data_available: 62+ dated circulars/orders (2014-2026) from GAD, DoIT&C, Administrative Reforms Department covering PAR appraisals, IPR (Immovable Property Return) filings, leave management, e-file processes, government accommodation allotment.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed live page with a reverse-chronological single-page list, each entry dated with title and PDF link, e.g. '11.12.2014 - Guidelines on Annual Performance Appraisal' through June 2026 entries on pending PARs. No pagination, no search.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Content is largely administrative/HR process circulars (leave, accommodation, appraisals) rather than substantive policy/procurement/corruption-relevant orders — lower investigative yield than expected; only 62 entries total, thin dataset; no structured metadata beyond title+date.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Static HTML list + PDF download

accepted_sources.name: West Bengal Mineral Development & Trading Corporation Ltd (WBMDTCL) Portal
accepted_sources.category: State Government Portals - East/Northeast (West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand, Assam, and NE states)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape tenders/notices pages and PDF documents (environmental clearances, empanelment). Investigate e-challan system for possible public lookup of mining transport permits (a common India investigative angle for illegal sand/coal mining).
accepted_sources.data_available: Tenders/procurement notices (EoI for CPO selection, agency empanelment for EC compliance), board of directors, coal allotment/mining project data by district (e.g. Birbhum), environmental clearance documents, SOP/user manuals, e-challan generation statistics (15.7M+ challans).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Live site with mixed-freshness content: recent tenders dated Aug-Sep 2025, static organizational pages, PDF environmental clearance docs, and an operational e-challan counter reflecting real-time mining transaction volume through July 2026 — indicates an active transactional backend relevant to illegal mining/royalty tracking investigations.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Site flags fraudulent domain impersonation issues (may indicate phishing confusion or portal migration instability); core organizational content is static/stale; e-challan system's public accessibility for querying individual transactions not yet confirmed — may require app-based access only.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State PSU portal with tender/PDF documents plus a separate mobile-app-gated transactional e-challan system

accepted_sources.name: Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Digital Repository
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: JSPUI/DSpace search interface scraping (HTML forms; DSpace may expose OAI-PMH); OCR text likely embedded in item records for scanned debates.
accepted_sources.data_available: OCR-searchable digitized archive (1921-present) of TN Legislative Council/Assembly debates, committee reports (Estimates, PAC, Rules, Privileges), bills, government resolutions, news clippings, and audio-visual/photo records. Bilingual English/Tamil search with filters by assembly number, date, business type, and member name.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch confirmed a live JSPUI/DSpace repository with dual-language search, advanced filters, and structured metadata (business classification, dates, member associations) covering historical and current legislative records back to 1921.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Bilingual OCR quality for older Tamil-language records may be poor; DSpace pagination and possible session/cookie handling for advanced search; large historical corpus needs incremental crawl strategy.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: DSpace/JSPUI repository scraper with OCR text extraction

accepted_sources.name: National eVidhan Application (NeVA) - State Assembly Portal Network
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Crawl the hub to enumerate per-state NeVA subdomains (e.g. mhla.neva.gov.in, wbla.neva.gov.in), then scrape each state's questions/bills/proceedings pages individually — likely varying templates per state instance.
accepted_sources.data_available: Central hub linking 28+ state legislative houses (assemblies and councils) covering proceedings, questions, bills, notices, session schedules, and committee reports. Distinct from Sansad which covers only Parliament.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch confirmed a live hub site listing state legislature links (Gujarat, TN, Haryana, UP, Bihar, and others), notice boards, session materials, multilingual support (12 languages), and downloadable mobile apps.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Each state instance may have a different UI/backend requiring per-state scraper logic; some state instances may require login for full document access; inconsistent data completeness across states.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Multi-tenant government portal crawler (per-subdomain adapters)

accepted_sources.name: Bihar Vidhan Sabha Online Question Reply Management System
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Crawl directory listing pages by session/period to enumerate PDF links, download PDFs, then OCR/text-extract (Hindi Devanagari) to parse question text, member name, department, and reply.
accepted_sources.data_available: Directory of downloadable PDFs of starred questions, short notice questions, and call attention notices organized by session (18th), period, question type, and date. Individual PDFs contain question numbers, member names, and subject matter with government replies.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch confirmed this is a document directory (not a queryable database) currently showing entries for the 18th Session, 2nd period, dated Feb 26, 2026, split into Hindi-labeled categories (starred/short-notice/call-attention) each linking to PDFs.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No structured search/API — pure PDF directory; Hindi-only PDFs need Devanagari OCR (poor OCR accuracy risk); no evident historical archive depth confirmed beyond current session in this fetch.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government PDF directory crawler + Hindi OCR pipeline

accepted_sources.name: ECI Electoral Trust Contribution Reports
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Same WAF-bypass browser automation approach as the main contribution reports; enumerate per-trust, per-year PDF file links from the category listing pages.
accepted_sources.data_available: Annual contribution reports filed by registered electoral trusts (e.g. Prudent Electoral Trust, Progressive Electoral Trust), organized by financial year from 2013-14 through recent years, tracing corporate donations funneled through trusts to parties.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Direct fetch blocked (403) but WebSearch confirmed live, actively-updated content: individual trust-specific PDF reports (e.g. 'Prudent Electoral Trust - Contribution Report FY 2020-21') hosted at eci.gov.in/files/file/... paths spanning at least 2013-14 to 2022-23+.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Same 403/WAF blocking as sibling ECI page; PDFs need to be individually enumerated and downloaded per trust/year; less-aggregated than ADR summaries so requires more manual cross-referencing to donor/company identities.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: WAF-protected government portal requiring browser automation bypass

accepted_sources.name: ECI Candidate Affidavit Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Browser automation to navigate election > accepted candidates listing, then bulk-download per-candidate affidavit PDFs; OCR/parse PDF forms for structured asset/criminal-case data.
accepted_sources.data_available: Candidate nomination affidavits (assets, liabilities, criminal cases, education) for contesting candidates, with affidavit management sections for received/accepted/rejected/withdrawn status per election.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Direct fetch blocked (403) but WebSearch confirmed the portal is live and actively used for current elections (referenced for 2026 assembly elections), with an 'Accepted' candidates list view and downloadable affidavit PDFs — this is the primary source MyNeta aggregates from.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Same WAF/403 blocking as other eci.gov.in subdomains; affidavits are scanned PDF forms requiring OCR (data not machine-readable natively); would need per-election, per-constituency enumeration to get a full candidate list.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: WAF-protected government portal requiring browser automation bypass

accepted_sources.name: MyNeta Declaration of Interest by Rajya Sabha Members
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: HTML scraping of paginated candidate index, then per-candidate profile page scraping; underlying original register forms are scanned images/PDFs requiring OCR to extract the actual directorship/shareholding text.
accepted_sources.data_available: Per-MP index (name, constituency/state, party, criminal cases, education, assets, liabilities) with clickable candidate profile pages; profiles link to digitized/scanned original Register of Members' Interest forms (directorships, shareholdings of controlling nature, paid consultancy) sourced from ADR/ECI.

Index lists current/ex-members (Rakesh Sinha-BJP, A K Antony-INC, Ahmed Patel-INC, Manmohan Singh-INC) each linking to detailed interest declaration scans.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Detailed interest data (directorships, shareholdings, consultancy) lives in scanned register images per member, not structured HTML on the index page - requires OCR. No bulk API/CSV export. The related ADR press-note URL for the same underlying data is metadata/summary-only and was rejected separately.

accepted_sources.obstacles: Individual report pages were not directly content-verified in this pass (only the index/menu was confirmed); need to fetch each of the 7 sub-report URLs to confirm live data population and pagination depth.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: MyNeta/ADR HTML index scrape + per-profile PDF/OCR pipeline

accepted_sources.obstacles: No bulk listing/API; must be queried via form parameters (likely POST with session state) to enumerate all orders; PDF text extraction needed per order for outcome/amount data; site copyright footer says 2018 which may indicate a stale template despite functional 2026 date filter

accepted_sources.confidence: High — content and structure directly confirmed via fetch

No sample FIR results were retrievable via passive fetch since the form requires an actual query submission; result field structure (FIR number, sections, date, status) unconfirmed.

accepted_sources.obstacles: No bulk export; must paginate across ~90-day windows and per-station to cover full history; potential anti-scraping/session tokens not confirmed without live browser test
accepted_sources.implementation_family: State police FIR portal scraper (ASPX form POST + pagination)

accepted_sources.name: India Justice Report - Consumer Justice Report 2026 + Consumer Courts Dashboard (ccdash)
accepted_sources.category: Meta Research - Datasets used by investigative journalists
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: PDF/infographic download for the report; dashboard appears to be a queryable web app (React/JS) - would need to check for underlying API calls or CSV export button via browser devtools for bulk extraction; otherwise scrape rendered tables.
accepted_sources.data_available: First comprehensive assessment of institutional capacity of India's Consumer Dispute Redressal Commissions (SCDRC/DCDRC) - budgets, infrastructure, HR vacancies, workload, gender diversity. Underlying case data: 28.57 lakh consumer cases filed 2010-2024, sourced from CONFONET/e-Jagriti. Companion interactive dashboard at ccdash.indiajusticereport.org shows case filed/pending/disposed counts, sector breakdown, disposal-time metrics, with 'Entity Search' and 'India View' geographic filtering, licensed CC-BY-NC 4.0.

Dashboard (ccdash.indiajusticereport.org) is live and interactive with national/state-level filters and an Entity Search feature, built from the erstwhile CONFONET data.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No visible direct bulk CSV/XLSX download of the underlying case-level data found on the report page itself - primary public artifacts are PDF report and an interactive dashboard rather than open bulk data; dashboard's data granularity (state/district/entity level) needs further probing to confirm depth before building an extractor.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Interactive JS dashboard scraping / PDF report parsing (same family as other India Justice Report outputs)

accepted_sources.name: DILRMP State RoR Web (Record of Rights portal directory)

accepted_sources.acquisition_method: N/A - not independently acquirable as a dataset; each linked state portal would need separate assessment (most require district/village/khasra number lookups, CAPTCHAs, no bulk export).

Covers land computerization status across ~95% of India's villages (6,25,137 of 6,57,397 villages digitized as of Dec 2023).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: WebFetch of the live page failed (ECONNRESET); search-result snippets confirm it is a links directory/table pointing to individual state land record portals (e.g., Bhulekh, Dharani, etc.) rather than a unified dataset or API of its own.
accepted_sources.obstacles: This is a meta-directory of links, not a data source itself - the real investigative value (if any) lies in each individual state RoR portal, which are 28+ separate heterogeneous government systems each requiring their own scraping approach, CAPTCHA handling, and often only support single-parcel lookup rather than bulk/API access. Rejecting as a distinct source; would need to evaluate specific state portals individually in a future batch.

accepted_sources.name: DGCIS — Statistics of Inland Coasting Trade / Foreign & Coastal Cargo Movement
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct PDF/Excel download of aggregate annual reports and table extraction (pdfplumber/camelot); separately investigate ftddp.dgciskol.gov.in for granular microdata behind login/subscription.
accepted_sources.data_available: Annual publications (2018-19 through 2023-24) of coastal/inland-coasting cargo statistics: vessel counts (steam/motor vs sailing) and commodity-wise quantity/value broken down by 12 maritime blocks (coastal states/UTs), freely downloadable as PDF (some years with Excel tables).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed real downloadable PDF 'Statistics of Foreign and Coastal Cargo Movements of India' (March 2025 edition, covering 2023-24): 17,969 vessel entries with cargo (5,864 steam/motor, 12,105 sailing) across the 12 maritime blocks. No login needed for these aggregate reports; a separate paid/login-gated portal (ftddp.dgciskol.gov.in) hosts more granular HS-code level foreign trade microdata under Official/Guest/Subscriber access tiers.
accepted_sources.obstacles: The freely available PDFs are only state-block aggregates limiting analysis to macro trend shifts rather than shipment or company-level tracing; the genuinely granular microdata sits behind a login/subscriber wall on ftddp.dgciskol.gov.in.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Scheduled PDF/Excel download plus table extraction for aggregate reports

accepted_sources.name: VAHAN NTR (parivahan services next-gen vehicle registry successor portal)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Requires headless-browser automation (JS rendering) to drive registration-number searches and paginate/query results, since it is a client-rendered SPA; useful for verifying vehicle ownership chains, fitness/insurance status, and hypothecation records tied to entities under investigation (e.g., seized-asset or benami vehicle checks).
accepted_sources.data_available: Successor platform to the legacy vahan.parivahan.gov.in vehicle/DL registry, covering ~23 crore vehicle records and ~11 crore driving-license records nationwide; supports registration-number based public search (masked owner info) plus authorized-user full detail lookup (chassis/engine number), and faceless RTO services (ownership transfer, duplicate RC, address change, hypothecation add/remove).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: The NTR URL itself returned only a bare 'NTR' string on fetch (JS-rendered SPA shell not executed by the fetch tool), so no actual search results or data fields were directly observed; existing knowledge and the legacy nrservices portal (already reachable, confirming ~377 million digitized vehicle records) corroborate the scale and general query capability, and the legacy portal explicitly directs users to migrate to this NTR URL as the vehicle/DL system of record going forward.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Public search is intentionally rate-limited/captcha-gated and masks owner names; full details require 'authorized user' credentials not available to the public; bulk/API access is not offered - this is a lookup-only interface, not a downloadable dataset, so value is per-record verification rather than bulk analysis.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Browser automation against JS SPA with captcha handling

Accompanying published research paper (India_Courts_In_Group_Bias.pdf) analyzing in-group bias in judicial decisions.

Raw case-level file format/size not shown on page — likely gated behind request to devdatalab.org.

Includes specific figures (e.g., Rs 858 crore for 'Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary' scheme in 2021-22).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched live platform page; confirmed two interactive 'Explorer' tools (Union and Assam) with real scheme-level rupee figures cited, plus links to related Medium/Substack analysis content.
