accepted_sources.name: IDS-DRR (Intelligent Data Solution for Disaster Risk Reduction) — CivicDataLab + Open Contracting Partnership
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Access live dashboard at drr.open-contracting.in for Assam district/sub-district reports; pull underlying pipeline code/data from GitHub (CivicDataLab/IDS-DRR-Assam-Risk-Model, CivicDataLab/IDS-DRR-Odisha) which include ETL scripts and likely output CSVs; combine tender-spend data with damage/hazard scores to identify disaster-fund misallocation.
accepted_sources.confidence: High — dashboard, data model, and GitHub pipeline all independently confirmed live with concrete field-level detail
accepted_sources.data_available: Integrated flood-risk platform joining government spending/tender data (SDRF, SOPD, RIDF, LTIF, CIDF disaster-fund tenders) with hazard/exposure/vulnerability datasets (satellite SAR flood inundation from Bhuvan/Sentinel, IMD rainfall, Mission Antyodaya household counts, WorldPOP population, NASADEM drainage density, schools/health-centre counts, crop/road/bridge/embankment damage records). Outputs monthly risk scores (1-5 scale) per revenue circle and district, currently live for Assam with Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh in progress/pilot (Bihar & UP pilot confirmed via Open Contracting Partnership Aug 2025 announcement).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched live dashboard homepage (confirmed interactive map, district/sub-district filters, dataset catalog by 4 categories) and the detailed data-model documentation page (civicdatalab-1.gitbook.io) which lists concrete field names (total_households, mean_rain, inundation_percentage, schools_count, total_tender_awarded_value, etc.) and confirms monthly CSV output per revenue circle.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Only Assam is fully live; other states marked 'Coming Soon' as of inspection. Full raw data model spans many source APIs (Bhuvan, IMD, WorldPOP) each with own access complexity if reproducing pipeline rather than using pre-built CSV outputs.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Multi-source ETL pipeline (Python) feeding a risk-scoring model, served via interactive GIS dashboard (Assam); raw pipeline and code hosted on GitHub per-state

accepted_sources.name: Justice Hub - Analysis of CALPRA Cases (2015-2023)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct HTTPS download of public CSV files from justicehub.in dataset resource URLs (CKAN-style portal), no auth required
accepted_sources.data_available: Case-level court registry data for ~10,800 cases under the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act (CALPRA), 1986, scraped from eCourts, covering Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Jan 2015-Mar 2023. Delivered as 5 linked CSVs (case_details.csv, case_transfers.csv, case_acts.csv, act.csv reference table, case_history.csv), a PDF data handbook defining variables, a ZIP of reclassification/standardization mappings, and a PDF research report ('Decoding data on Implementation'). CC BY 4.0, uploaded by Apoorv Anand (Enfold Proactive Health Trust).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched case_details.csv directly and confirmed real rows: columns include cino (unique case ID), case_no, court_name, district/state names+codes, dt_regis, fir_no/fir_year, police_station, judge designation (desgname), disposal nature/outcome classification, judgment_date/link, case-type reclassification fields. Sample rows show real cases e.g. CJM Bongaigaon (Assam) case ASBN030004442020 disposed 'Withdrawal', UP Bhadohi cases 'SETTLED IN LOK ADALAT', Bihar Araria cases still 'Pending' since 2016-2017 -- exposing multi-year pendency and settlement/withdrawal patterns not visible in NCRB aggregate stats (dataset notes NCRB reported only 1,329 CALPRA cases 2015-2022 vs 9,193 eCourts trials found -- a major reporting-gap story in itself).
accepted_sources.obstacles: None for the CSVs -- clean, well-documented, CC BY 4.0. The two companion PDF reports are image/design-heavy (Adobe Photoshop-produced, JP2/DCTDecode embedded images) with no text layer, so OCR would be needed to extract report narrative/statistics beyond what's in the raw CSVs; not a blocker since the CSVs are the real data asset.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: csv_download

accepted_sources.name: Justice Hub - Analysis of PCMA Cases (2015-2023)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: PDF report is a direct download; for structured/queryable data, extract child_marriage=1 rows from the CALPRA dataset's case_details.csv (same eCourts scrape, shared resource group) rather than the PCMA dataset page itself
accepted_sources.data_available: Report analyzing 174 judgments under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 2006 across Assam, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu (Jan 2015-Jan 2023), sourced from eCourts. Delivered primarily as a single PDF report ('Trends in Child Marriage'). Note: case-level PCMA CSVs (case_details etc.) are bundled together with CALPRA data under the same underlying eCourts scrape/resource group as the CALPRA dataset (case_details.csv contains a child_marriage/pcma_type_name_reclassification columns), so the raw PCMA case data is effectively obtainable via the CALPRA dataset's CSVs filtered on child_marriage=1.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched the PDF report directly (report2-childmarriage_web.pdf, 2.4MB, 38 pages) -- confirmed it is a real, live, downloadable document, but it is image-based (Adobe Photoshop-exported, JP2 compressed images, no extractable text layer), so automated text/data extraction failed via standard PDF fetch. The underlying case-level rows for PCMA are present as columns (child_marriage flag, pcma_type_name_reclassification_1/2/3) inside the CALPRA dataset's case_details.csv, which was directly inspected and confirmed to contain real rows.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Report PDF has no text layer (design/infographic style) -- requires OCR (e.g. Tesseract on rendered pages, or Adobe/Acrobat OCR) to pull out narrative statistics, tables, and quotes. Raw case-level PCMA data is not offered as a standalone CSV on the PCMA dataset page itself; must be derived by filtering the CALPRA dataset's case_details.csv on child_marriage/pcma flags.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: pdf_ocr_plus_csv_filter

accepted_sources.name: DGCIS Foreign Trade Data Dissemination Portal (FTDDP) - Guest Mode
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Navigate to guest query hash-routes (Angular SPA: #!/guestsearchquery, #!/guestmonthlytimeseries, #!/gueststateoforigin, #!/guestdistrictoforigin) which call backend REST endpoints for HS-code/state/district export-import data; drive with a headless browser or reverse-engineer the underlying JSON API calls.
accepted_sources.confidence: medium-high: portal and guest routes confirmed live and reachable without login; exact JSON API shape not yet captured, would need a browser-driven follow-up session
accepted_sources.data_available: Free, no-login Guest query modules confirmed live: guestsearchquery (commodity/HS-code search), guestmonthlytimeseries, guestyearlytimeseries, gueststateoforigin, guestdistrictoforigin. Provides principal-commodity and up to 8-digit HS-code level export/import statistics with state and district of origin breakdowns, updated monthly, from DGCI&S (Ministry of Commerce), India's authoritative trade statistics body.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched guestindex.html directly (19.5KB): confirmed five distinct guest-accessible query links requiring no login, plus a public user manual and policy PDFs (Data_dissemination_policy.pdf, META_DATA.pdf, PC_composition_HSN2012/2017/2022.pdf) documenting 2/4/6/8-digit HS-level and principal-commodity dissemination free for the trailing ~24 months. The fully authenticated Official/Subscriber tier holds finer data but is gated and was not accessed.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Angular SPA - raw HTML fetch only returns the app shell, so a headless browser (or network-tab API reverse engineering) is required to pull real numbers. Guest tier is capped at aggregated commodity/state/district level for ~24 trailing months only; no transaction, shipping-bill, or company/IEC-level data (paid Subscriber tier only) - useful for macro/regional trade-flow stories, not firm-specific customs tracing.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: government_trade_statistics_spa

accepted_sources.name: RTI Rajasthan - Second Appeal Status Search (public report tool)
accepted_sources.category: State Government Portals - North / RTI Transparency
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Reverse-engineer the Angular main.js bundle to find the exact REST endpoint the WebsecondappealreportComponent posts appeal numbers to (under rtiapi/api/), then script batch queries by appeal number/range or via bulk report exports if available; alternatively drive with a headless browser and submit the visible search form.
accepted_sources.confidence: medium: page and search widget confirmed live and public; exact bulk-query capability of the underlying API not yet verified
accepted_sources.data_available: A public, no-login search widget for looking up RTI second-appeal status by appeal number (single text-input form calling a backend REST API under rtiapi/api/). Separate authenticated citizen sections exist for filing/tracking (admin/citisaredirect) but the report/status lookup page itself does not require login.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Fetched the raw HTML (6.2KB) - confirms this is an Angular SPA (runtime.js/main.js/polyfills.js/vendor.js bundle, ~1.7MB main.js). Decompiled main.js to locate the WebsecondappealreportComponent, which renders a bootstrap form-group with a text input bound via ngModel and a submit button - i.e., a genuine public case-status search tool, not a dead page. Confirmed API namespace rtiapi/api/ and document repository rtiapi/FIleManager/Documents/ (SPIO/FAO/IC contact lists, citizen guidance PDFs) also live.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Confirmed as an Angular SPA (previously logged as a 'parse error' in earlier attempts - resolved: raw fetch returns only the JS-rendering shell, must inspect main.js or use a browser). Search appears to require a specific appeal number rather than free-text/date-range browsing, which limits bulk discovery unless an internal listing/report endpoint is also exposed - needs a follow-up session with a headless browser to capture the live network calls and confirm bulk-listing capability.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: government_case_status_spa

accepted_sources.name: WBOCMMS - West Bengal Online Consent Management & Monitoring System
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Automated form-submit/scrape of search results pages across date ranges and districts; individual record pages via industryRegMaster/show/{id} sequential or discovered IDs
accepted_sources.data_available: Publicly searchable database of environmental Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) applications granted to industries/mining operations in West Bengal, run by WB Pollution Control Board. Searchable by industry name (first letter), application ID, date range, application type (CTO/CTE), pollution category (air/water/both), regional office/DIC (13 regional + 21 district offices), and certificate status (New/Renew/AutoRenew).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Search result table includes: serial number, application number, application name (industry), application type, district, application submission date, granted date, pollution category, certificate type, consent order details. Confirmed live search interface at grantedApplicationSearchEODB and industryRegMaster/show/{id} record pages (e.g. record 86670 for WBMDTCL). Note: this is an environmental consent registry, not a dedicated 'minor mineral mining license' system as originally suggested -- it covers all industries requiring pollution consent, including mining/mineral operators.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Certificate self-signed on www subdomain (must use bare wbocmms.nic.in, not www.); search requires POST params per district/date range to enumerate full dataset; no bulk export/API found; results appear only after search execution
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government consent/licensing registry - form search + tabular results (ASP.NET/JSP-based, non-SPA)

accepted_sources.name: WB Industries Department - WBMDTCL Mining RFP/EOI Documents
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct PDF download from known /files/Mines/ path plus targeted search-engine discovery of additional filenames (no directory listing found); PDF text extraction
accepted_sources.data_available: Publicly downloadable PDF tender documents (RFPs, EOIs, Corrigendums) issued by West Bengal Mineral Development and Trading Corporation Ltd (WBMDTCL) for sand mining block auctions and Mine Developer-Operator empanelment, hosted under the WB Dept of Industry, Commerce & Enterprises site.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed real PDFs: PURBN_3_23032023_A01_RFP.pdf (sand mining RFP defining Mine Plan Approval, Environment Clearance, Forest Clearance, Consent to Establish/Operate requirements), EOI_CAT_B_06042023.pdf (empanelment of sand-mine excavation Operators in 2 categories), CorrigendumCatB.pdf (bidder eligibility clarifications e.g. LLP structure). Documents include fee schedules (Rs 17,700 RFP document fee), bidder obligations, and mine block details.
accepted_sources.obstacles: SSL certificate verification issues on some fetch tools (self-signed/misconfigured chain); no directory index -- must discover filenames via search engines or WBMDTCL 'whats_current' notice pages; low update frequency; scattered across ad hoc filenames with no consistent naming convention or API
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Static PDF tender document corpus, discovery via search + notice pages

accepted_sources.name: CivicDataLab / HAQ - Data4Justice POCSO Case Tracking Dataset
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct ZIP/PDF download from Justice Hub dataset page; supplement with live Superset dashboard (may require separate access) and GitHub repo CivicDataLab/POCSO_case_law_analysis for case-law analysis code/data
accepted_sources.data_available: Curated case-level dataset of 19,783 POCSO Act cases (2012-2020) from district courts in Assam, Delhi and Haryana, scraped from the eCourts Case Information System, with accompanying data dictionary/codebook, data handbook (directory structure), state-level factsheets, and a live Superset dashboard (POCSO caselaw tracker) at superset.civicdatalab.in/superset/dashboard/52/.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Dataset page confirms downloadable ZIP archive of case records plus PDF research report and state factsheets; documentation references case registration details, trial proceedings, and case outcomes/disposal nature per case. A companion Substack analysis piece (dataforjustice.substack.com) discusses trial duration and disposal-type statistics derived from this same dataset, corroborating real structured content behind it.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data is static/historical (only through April 2020, not continuously updated); need to confirm Superset dashboard requires login; underlying eCourts source data was manually curated for a one-off research project, not a live feed
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Static curated dataset (ZIP/CSV + PDF documentation), one-time download

accepted_sources.name: DILRMP State-wise Land Records Computerization Dataset (via data.gov.in OGD mirror)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Bulk CSV/JSON/XML download or OGD API (api key + resource_id) from data.gov.in resource pages; for finer district-level and more current data, use browser automation against dilrmp.gov.in MIS report pages with statecode query parameters.
accepted_sources.data_available: State/UT-wise physical progress on DILRMP components: Computerization of Record of Rights (RoR), Registration computerization, SRO-Land Records integration, modern record rooms, survey/resurvey using modern technology. This resource covers Northeast states 2021-22 to 2025-26; a related resource on the same platform (stateut-wise-details-computerization-land-records-clr) covers all-India CLR data as of a Dec 2024 Lok Sabha reply. Underlying live source is the DILRMP-MIS portal (dilrmp.gov.in) with state and district-level drill-down report pages.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed data.gov.in resource page loads (HTTP 200, ~1MB HTML), titled 'State-wise Details of Various Components/Activities of DILRMP in Northeast States from 2021-22 to 2025-26', tagged to Ministry of Electronics & IT / Rural Development, page contains numerous download/csv/api references consistent with data.gov.in's standard CSV/JSON/XML export plus OGD API. The primary live source, dilrmp.gov.in's JSF-based state/district report pages (e.g. rptComputerizationOfLandRecord.xhtml, dashboard/state-list-dashboard), repeatedly failed to load via direct fetch (connection reset / timeout), indicating a heavier session-based ASP/JSF app not reliably scrapable without full browser automation - data.gov.in is the practical acquisition path though it is a periodic snapshot, not live.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Primary source (dilrmp.gov.in) is a slow, session-based JSF government portal returning connection resets on plain HTTP fetch - requires headless browser or retry logic. data.gov.in mirror is periodic (not real-time) and geographically partial in the specific resource inspected (Northeast states only; full India version exists as a separate resource).
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Government open-data portal (data.gov.in OGD API/CSV) with optional fallback to JSF report-portal scraping (browser automation) for live/granular district data

accepted_sources.name: CivicDataLab - Analysing Implementation of Child Protection Laws in India (project hub, incl. PCMA dataset)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Navigate from project hub to Justice Hub CKAN dataset pages, then direct CSV download
accepted_sources.data_available: Project page linking to two Justice Hub datasets: CALPRA (2015-2023, 6 states, ~10,800 cases) and PCMA/Prohibition of Child Marriage Act analysis (174 judgments, 3 states: Assam, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Jan 2015-Jan 2023). Also links a related POCSO tracking dataset (see related_sources) covering Assam, Delhi, Haryana 2012-2020 eCourts data. Research reports, methodology write-ups (Medium/Patrick J. McGovern Foundation), and CC BY 4.0 licensed CSVs hosted on Justice Hub.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Verified underlying CALPRA CSV is real and downloadable (see above). Page itself is a project/methodology hub rather than a raw data page, but all data assets it points to were confirmed live on justicehub.in.
accepted_sources.obstacles: The project page itself has no direct downloads; must follow through to Justice Hub for actual data (already validated)
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Static CSV/PDF bulk download (CKAN data portal), same pipeline as CALPRA

accepted_sources.name: DAKSH's Database on Judicial Data / DAKSH High Court Data Portal
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct CSV download from Justice Hub for the completeness/mapping tables; for full raw case-level records, use DAKSH High Court Data Portal (database.dakshindia.org) dashboards + Dropbox bulk downloads (may require locating current Dropbox links per dashboard)
accepted_sources.data_available: 3 CSVs (Civilcriminalmapping.csv, StagesMapping.csv, Databaseppln.csv) plus 'Report on Deciphering Judicial Data.pdf' on Justice Hub, covering All-India eCourts data 2007-2020 on case-type classification, procedural stage mapping, and per-state field completeness. Separately, the live DAKSH High Court Data Portal (database.dakshindia.org) offers dashboards (Writ cases, Bail applications, Tax matters) plus bulk CSV downloads via Dropbox links (CC BY-NC 4.0), with a Data Guidebook describing full case/hearing schema (CNR number, petitioner/respondent, judge names, acts/sections, hearing purpose, disposal nature, advocate names, etc).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Downloaded Databaseppln.csv directly (30 rows, one per state) showing percentage data-completeness of ~33 case/hearing fields (CNR number, petitioner, respondent, judge names, under_acts/sections, disposal nature, advocate names) sourced from eCourts/NJDG per state, e.g. Andhra Pradesh 100% on most fields but only 27.63% on 'police_station'. This confirms the underlying live database schema is rich case-level judicial data, though this particular resource is a completeness-metadata table rather than raw case rows.
accepted_sources.obstacles: The Justice Hub CSVs are useful metadata/mapping tables, not raw case records; full raw case-level bulk data lives on database.dakshindia.org via Dropbox links that need to be located per dashboard (Writ/Bail/Tax), adding a discovery step
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Static CSV bulk download (CKAN) for metadata tables; dashboard + Dropbox bulk download for full raw High Court case data

accepted_sources.name: WB Industries Department Portal - Mining RFP/EOI Documents (wbindustries.gov.in)
accepted_sources.category: Procurement / Mining Tenders (State Government - West Bengal)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Scrape the whats_current.html listing page and /files/Mines/ directory for PDF links; parse PDFs for mine names, bidder eligibility, MDO awardees, financial/royalty terms and clearance conditions. Cross-reference awarded MDOs against company ownership/political-linkage databases (MCA21, MyNeta) for conflict-of-interest checks.
accepted_sources.data_available: PDF notices for RFPs and Expressions of Interest issued by WBMDTCL (West Bengal Mineral Development and Trading Corporation) for sand and coal mining, including Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) empanelment, mine plan approvals, environmental/forest clearance requirements, contract tenure and eligibility criteria for bidders. Files are hosted under /files/Mines/ with naming like PUR_12_07012023_A01.pdf, EOI_CAT_B_06042023.pdf.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Verified via web search results and cached PDF titles: WBMDTCL EOI for empanelment of Operators for sand mine excavation across two bidder categories, 5-year Sand Mining Agreement tenure, MDO responsible for Mine Plan Approval/Environmental Clearance/Forest Clearance and transport/stocking/loading of sand. Multiple dated EOI/tender PDFs found (e.g. EOI_CAT_B_06042023.pdf, PUR_12_07012023_A01.pdf).
accepted_sources.obstacles: WebFetch repeatedly failed with TLS certificate errors on wbindustries.gov.in (both https and http) in this session, suggesting a misconfigured/self-signed cert typical of NIC-hosted state portals — a real access obstacle requiring a scraper that ignores/handles cert verification. No structured API; must enumerate PDF links from static HTML and parse PDF text.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: PDF scraping + link enumeration from static gov portal with TLS quirks

accepted_sources.name: MSTC WBMDTCL Coal E-Auction Records (mstcindia.co.in)
accepted_sources.category: State PSU E-Auction / Natural Resource Allocation Records
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Enumerate auction catalog report URLs (pattern: 'Auction Catalog Report <id>.htm') under /mstc_static_pages/coal/WBMDTCL/ and scrape lot-level tables; historical catalogs appear to persist as static pages so a crawl of the directory/sitemap could recover years of coal allocation records for cross-referencing against buyer companies and pricing anomalies.

Registration/EMD procedure pages and scheme PDFs also present.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed real lot-level data: Lot 01, G4 ROM, 5,000 MT, GCV 6101-6400 KCAL/KG, sourced from Trans Damodar OCP Barjora Bankura colliery, auction held Nov 6 2012 14:30-16:30, inspection window Oct 20-Nov 5 2012, reserve-price-plus-increment bidding rules disclosed. The specific 'WBMDTCL Delivery of Coal' page checked contained only an operational notice (one-day suspension), not transaction data — auction catalog pages are the actual data source, not the delivery-notice pages.
accepted_sources.obstacles: No index/API — catalog pages use unpredictable numeric IDs in filenames, so discovery requires crawling internal links or Google-dorking site: for the full archive. Buyer identity and final winning bid price are not shown on the catalog page itself (only lot/reserve terms) — final results may be on a separate results page not yet located.

accepted_sources.sample_summary: Verified the GitHub repo justicehub-in/budgets-for-justice-datasets/datasets/state-budgets/assam contains 19 real committed files including all_heads_list.csv, budget_timeseries.csv, budget_timeseries_updated_2022.csv, code_level_summary.csv, major_head_coverage.csv plus an xlsx and a files-for-viz subfolder — this is genuine tabular budget data, not just frontend code, satisfying the CivicDataLab data-file requirement.

accepted_sources.name: Rajasthan State Information Commission (RIC) Second Appeal Decisions/Orders
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: ASP.NET WebForms scraping with session/viewstate handling (possibly requiring a headless browser like Playwright) to page through the decisions archive; alternatively query StatusOfSecondAppeal.aspx by department/date range if such filters exist. Cross-reference against MyNeta/Sansad style department accountability angle: identify which departments/officials are repeat RTI violators and where commissioners imposed penalties.

accepted_sources.obstacles: Table content did not render via simple HTTP fetch (likely JS/postback-driven); may need cookie/session persistence across requests; large backlog of years to page through; no evident bulk export or API.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: aspnet-postback-scrape

accepted_sources.name: CivicDataLab flood-data-ecosystem-Himachal-Pradesh (TENDERS + HPSDMA modules)

Sources/HPSDMA/data/SDRF has cleaned_sdrf_with_final_amount.csv (5.6MB) — State Disaster Response Fund relief and mitigation disbursements by district, plus HPSDMA/PDNA/PDNA-2025 post-disaster needs assessment folder and losses-and-damages Raw/Loss Data folders. accepted_sources.name: Indian High Court Judgments (AWS Open Data / eCourts corpus)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct S3 bulk download (aws s3 cp/sync, no-sign-request) or Athena SQL over Parquet metadata for filtering by court/date/case-type before pulling PDFs.
accepted_sources.data_available: s3://indian-high-court-judgments — full judgment PDFs plus raw metadata (JSON) and structured metadata (Parquet) for 25 Indian High Courts, updated quarterly, individual PDFs and bulk tar archives, CC-BY-4.0, no AWS account/credentials needed (--no-sign-request).
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Registry page confirms schema.org Dataset entry with license CC-BY-4.0, source org Dattam Labs, and documented access via `aws s3 sync s3://indian-high-court-judgments/data/tar/`; companion GitHub repo (vanga/indian-high-court-judgments) provides dataset.md docs, Athena SQL tutorials for querying structured metadata, and full-text extraction guides.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Very large corpus (~1TB) — investigative use requires targeted Athena queries to narrow before bulk PDF retrieval; judgment text is in scanned/native PDFs so cross-court entity extraction (litigant names, companies, judges) needs an OCR/NLP pipeline layered on top.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: s3-bulk-dataset

accepted_sources.name: CivicDataLab POCSO Case Law Analysis (GitHub repo) + Data4Justice POCSO datasets (Justice Hub)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Direct raw GitHub CSV download (raw.githubusercontent.com, no auth) for the case-law repo; ZIP download from Justice Hub CKAN-style dataset page for the 19,783-case Data4Justice district court dataset.
accepted_sources.data_available: GitHub repo contains real committed data files: processed_judgements.csv (13.1MB, full judgement text with fields id, text, language, victim_age, victim_age_bucket, convicted_count, acquitted_count, order_verb_adj, judgement_verb_adj, document, judgement_year) and date_wise_cases.csv (64KB, daily case registration/decision/filing counts from 2013). Also includes R analysis scripts and a Superset dashboard config. Separately, the Justice Hub dataset page for the HAQ Centre for Child Rights / CivicDataLab #Data4Justice project (AGAMI Data for Justice Challenge funded) offers a downloadable ZIP of case-level data for 19,783 POCSO cases from district courts in Assam, Delhi and Haryana (2012-2020), a Data Handbook, state factsheets, and a HAQ factbook profiling 417 children in cases.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: processed_judgements.csv sample row: id 0fd84e310cbdad4bbe8b4bddb2a73892_MHTH250012952017 with full order text of a POCSO S.156(3) application naming accused, offence sections (366A/375/376 IPC + POCSO), plus derived fields for victim age bucket and conviction/acquittal/outcome classification. date_wise_cases.csv gives day-level counts of cases registered/decided/filed from 2013 onward. Justice Hub page confirms downloadable ZIP with case-level data for 19,783 district-court POCSO cases across 3 states/UT, 2012-2020, plus PDF factsheets and data handbook.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Data is static/one-time (2020-2021 vintage snapshot, not live-updating). processed_judgements.csv text has scrape/formatting artifacts (e.g. 'POSCO' misspellings) requiring cleanup; case coverage limited to 3 states (Assam, Delhi, Haryana) for the district-court dataset, not national.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: CSV/ZIP bulk download via HTTP (GitHub raw + CKAN resource download), no auth or JS rendering needed

accepted_sources.name: DAKSH High Court Data Portal (Writ, Bail, Tax dashboards + Dropbox bulk datasets)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Dropbox shared-folder bulk download (public link, no login) for underlying CSVs; dashboard pages themselves are server-rendered pages describing pre-aggregated stats, would need separate scraping if per-case detail beyond the Dropbox CSVs is desired.
accepted_sources.data_available: Live dashboards for Writ cases (database.dakshindia.org/writ/), Bail cases (bail-dashboard/) covering 927,896 bail cases filed 2010-2021, and a Tax litigation dashboard (introduction-to-tax-matters-at-high-courts/), all built from eCourts-scraped High Court data covering 23 of 25 High Courts since 2015. A 'Resources' menu links to two public Dropbox folders: one a Data Guidebook (data dictionary/field definitions) and one the actual cleaned CSV datasets used in the dashboards, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Dashboard pages describe metrics on bail case types, durations and outcomes, and writ case subject matter, sourced from the eCourts mobile app scrape. The Dropbox bulk-dataset link (confirmed live, HTTP 302 redirect to a real Dropbox share) is the actual download path for the underlying CSVs referenced by the dashboards; individual page fetches did not expose file-level names/sizes but confirm the download mechanism is live and public.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Dropbox share links can rotate/expire and are not a stable API; dashboards are pre-aggregated (not raw case-level unless the Dropbox CSVs contain case-level rows, which requires downloading the actual archive to confirm field granularity); site coverage is only High Courts (not district courts), and updates cadence is unclear (last confirmed activity discussions circa 2023 LinkedIn post).
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Dropbox shared-folder bulk CSV download; dashboard scraping would be static HTML/JS charts

accepted_sources.name: CEO Haryana Candidate Affidavits (DynamicContentId CMS listing)
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: POST to /WebCMS/GetDynamicContentListData with known DynamicTypeId/WebsiteId to enumerate affidavit-related entries; recurse into each entry's DynamicTypeIdView to reach constituency-wise pages, scrape ContentFile/FinalFile PDF links, then download/OCR affidavits for candidate assets, criminal cases, and education history.
accepted_sources.confidence: medium-high — endpoint verified live and returns real structured data, but full constituency-level PDF paths not yet traced end-to-end in this pass
accepted_sources.data_available: JSON list of election/affidavit content entries (title, publication date, external links, and for leaf constituency listings: ContentFile/ActionFile/FinalFile fields holding PDF paths to candidate nomination/affidavit documents) served by the CMS backend behind the public 'Affidavits of Candidates' page.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed the page's grid is populated via POST /WebCMS/GetDynamicContentListData with _DynamicTypeId=54&_WebsiteId=24&_IsArchieved=false — no auth/CSRF needed, tested directly with curl and got 200 with real JSON. Sample entries returned: {'DynamicContentId':1686,'Title':'Biennial Election to Council of States (Rajya Sabha), 2026','ExternalLink':'https://www.ceoharyana.gov.in/WebCMS/Start/1975',...} plus similar entries for the Dec 2024 Rajya Sabha bye-election and general elections. Each entry links to /WebCMS/Start/?Id=1462&DynamicTypeIdView={DynamicContentId}, which for constituency-level pages resolves to candidate affidavit/nomination PDF download links (ContentFile/FinalFile schema fields populated at leaf nodes).
accepted_sources.obstacles: Requires walking a nested DynamicTypeId tree (constituency lists sit under further DynamicTypeIdView layers) to reach leaf nodes with actual PDFs; affidavit PDFs are scanned Form-26 documents needing OCR; DynamicTypeId values for other election cycles/states use the same CMS platform (devitsandbox mirror seen) so IDs must be re-derived per election.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: CMS JSON API enumeration + PDF OCR

accepted_sources.name: Assam State Budget Line-Item Datasets — Budgets for Justice (Justice Hub)

accepted_sources.confidence: high — actual row-level data independently fetched and inspected, not just repo metadata

accepted_sources.name: Rajasthan RTI Second Appeal / Aging-Pendency Report API
accepted_sources.category: State Government Portals - North / RTI Transparency
accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Reverse-engineer exact endpoint path/params for GetAgingCumPendencySecondAppealsReport and sibling report methods from the Angular service class in main.js (webpack bundle), then call rtiapi/api/<endpoint> directly with department/date-range params to pull structured pendency/appeal statistics without browser rendering.
accepted_sources.confidence: medium — real API base and service/method names confirmed from source, but exact working request not yet executed successfully
accepted_sources.data_available: Backend REST API (rtiapi/api/) feeding SPA report components: RptsecondappealComponent (second appeal register), WebsecondappealreportComponent (aging/pendency of second appeals by department), WebfirstappealreportComponent, WebapplicationreportComponent, WebcomplaintreportComponent — implying department-wise/date-wise RTI application, first-appeal, second-appeal and complaint statistics are queryable.
accepted_sources.sample_summary: Confirmed the site (https://rti.rajasthan.gov.in/websecondappealreport) is an Angular app-root SPA that WebFetch cannot render, but downloaded and grepped the compiled main.js (1.7MB) bundle directly. Found the real API base 'https://rti.rajasthan.gov.in/rtiapi/api/' (alongside internal dev URLs http://10.68.231.220/RTIAPI2/api/ and localhost, confirming this is the genuine backend, not a decoy) and located the live call site 'this.reportService.GetAgingCumPendencySecondAppealsReport(data).subscribe(...)' plus sibling report components for first appeals, applications, and complaints — all backed by the same rtiapi.
accepted_sources.obstacles: Exact REST path suffix and required request payload not yet isolated (minified webpack bundle needs deeper static analysis or a Playwright session to sniff the live XHR); may require session/auth token for some report endpoints even though the API base itself was reachable.
accepted_sources.implementation_family: Angular SPA reverse-engineered REST API

accepted_sources.name: DDL Judicial Data Portal (Development Data Lab) - 81M district court cases, judge-level data

accepted_sources.acquisition_method: Manual/browser-driven Dropbox folder access (or rclone/dropbox API with a real browser session) to enumerate and download CSVs; cross-reference judge and case metadata via linked Google Sheets mentioned on the landing page.

The devdatalab.org/judicial-data page explicitly describes the download folder structure (cases, judges, act sections, via linked Google Sheets) and points to a Dropbox share link, but the Dropbox page rendered only a bare 'Dropbox' placeholder under automated fetch (likely JS-gated listing), so actual file contents/sizes were not directly verified.

rejected_sources.name: FCRA foreign-contribution disclosures (FC-4 annual returns / donor-wise received)
rejected_sources.reason: Blocked source — 2026-07-13. The old fcraonline.nic.in ASP.NET portal is retired: all *.aspx report pages (incl. the once-public fc3_amount.aspx 'Foreign Contribution received - quarterwise' and fc_ann_return_all.aspx) now 307-redirect to a React/Vite SPA at fcraonline.gov.in. The SPA's backend is a clean REST API, but the openly-fetchable no-auth endpoints expose only aggregate counts (/api/hpdashboard/*) and an FCRA-registration DIRECTORY (POST /api/filterasso/getFilterData, modes YEAR/STATE_DIST) returning RegistrationNo/AssociationName/Address/Nature and nothing else — no amounts, no donors, no per-year FC-received figures. The actual foreign-contribution money trail (FC-4 annual returns / donor-wise received) is authentication-gated: GET /api/dashboard/annual-returns returns HTTP 401 'Authentication failed' (association login/OTP), and no public /api/public/* endpoint serves any amount or donor. So the disclosure DATA the source is wanted for is unreachable; only the registered-NGO directory is fetchable, which is not the money-from-abroad trail. Revisit if MHA republishes the public FC-received report or exposes a public FC-4 amount endpoint. (An open FCRA-registered-NGO directory json-api — id fcra_associations — could be wired as a weaker org-directory source if desired, but it carries no amounts/donors.)

Tested directly with curl (cookie jar preserved across GET+POST): every POST attempt redirected to login. No public/unauthenticated path to actual granted-application result rows exists; the visible form is a decoy shell without valid credentials. Rejected per instruction to reject sources with no realistic extraction path.

rejected_sources.name: CIC — Central Information Commission decisions (name search)
rejected_sources.reason: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-15 (prior reject stands). The only route to the CIC decision corpus is a CAPTCHA-gated POST search form on dsscic.nic.in (fields incl. captcha[required] + _csrfToken); POST without a solved captcha returns HTTP 403. No static <a href> PDF listing, no <table> in raw HTML, no data.gov.in bulk mirror — pdf-archive/readBodies has nothing to harvest. Solving the CAPTCHA = bot-detection this project must not run. Sole clean artifact is one static 77.7MB curated decision-compendium PDF (cic.gov.in/sites/default/files/cicdecisioncompedium.pdf) — landmark decisions only, not the live stream; low incremental value, not wired.

rejected_sources.name: NGO Darpan (NITI Aayog) — NGO/VO registry
rejected_sources.reason: VERIFIED 2026-07-15 un-ingestable. Angular SPA; every /apis/ endpoint returns 401 without a client-computed AES-GCM signature+requid header (static signKey handshake via capis/sys-id), and the NGO search (regis/ngos) additionally requires a per-query 6-char image CAPTCHA (capis/captcha). Bypassing the request-signing + per-query CAPTCHA = bot-detection the project must not run. No data.gov.in/OGD mirror of the per-NGO registry exists.

rejected_sources.name: NDAP — National Data & Analytics Platform (NITI Aayog)
rejected_sources.reason: VERIFIED 2026-07-15: not a wireable source, it is a DISCOVERY LAYER. Frontend is a create-react-app JS shell; backend loadqa.ndapapi.com/v1/* is a custom POST-only JSON API requiring a registered API key (unauthenticated calls return 405 / Invalid Request). No anonymous bulk/CSV download. Correct use: browse NDAP to identify relevant datasets (MGNREGA, State Finances/Budgets, DBT, GST, Public Finance Stats), then ingest each specific dataset via data.gov.in using the existing ogd-resource/ckan-datastore kinds keyed by DATA_GOV_API_KEY — not NDAP itself.

run_history.note: Resolved 4 accept/reject contradictions from cross-run duplicate discovery: KPPP, IREPS, Sagarmala kept accepted (real content found in at least one pass, other rejection was stale/subjective/transient); WBHRC dropped from accepted (both passes agree it has no bulk-queryable data).

Resolved 3 more accept/reject contradictions found after first cleanup pass: ECI Candidate Affidavit Portal and Bhoomi Karnataka kept accepted (consistent with sibling WAF-blocked/lookup-only sources already accepted this project); NGDRS dropped from accepted (both passes independently confirmed no public record-level search exists, aggregate-only).

Resolved 4 more accept/reject contradictions from Run 6 (leads batch): all converged on reject (Jan Soochna's own accepted-entry text admits no bulk export; Silpasathi/RAJ ORDERS have aggregate-only or low-signal content per both passes; Zombie Tracker live-site direct inspection found no visible database vs. only corroborating evidence for acceptance). Dropped from accepted: Jan Soochna Portal (Rajasthan) - Scheme & Beneficiary Data; Silpasathi Portal (West Bengal Single Window Industrial Clearance); RAJ ORDERS (rajorders.com)

Dropped CivicDataLab Zombie Tracker (zombietracker.in) from accepted — the rejected pass did deeper verification (checked linked GitHub repo directly, found no committed data files) while the accepted pass admits it never scraped the live case table.

Resolved 6 accept/reject contradictions from Run 7. Rejected (kept as rejected, dropped accepted dup): DILRMP CLR dashboard (both passes never actually loaded content — connection failures only), WB DMM (unreachable both times, only weak corroborating-search evidence), Judicial Data Collaborative (confirmed link-directory/meta-index, not primary data), oci-assam-frontend (accepted entrys own text admits platform is undeployed/brainstorming-phase, self-contradicting). Accepted (kept, dropped stale rejection): POCSO_case_law_analysis GitHub repo and child-protection-research project page — the accepted pass fetched the raw CSV directly and found real case-level data (named POCSO judgment rows) that the rejecting pass missed by only checking repo file listing.
